UC labels below are stable draft handles only. Canonical storage uses numeric UseCaseId; do NOT invent string database UC IDs. Required plugin client.UseCases List/Get/Create/flows/actors/LinkFr/GetCoverage operations under canonical O workspace in Act after approval. Read-only searches RunAs, Agent Help, service update and agent execution returned empty; exact title/product/FR-linked lookup before creation may identify an existing UC to UPDATE instead of NEW. Such disposition and canonical numeric-ID map must be listed in the approved catalog before product tests; no duplicate or guessed linkage. Preserve historical actor/flow order. Realizes links to every listed FR; AC references explicit in flow step notes, not assumed from FR link alone. UC basic/alternative/exception flows must be stored with separate ordered steps and named actor IDs (not header-only shell creation). Any server surface unavailable blocks canonical capture, not permission to raw-edit store.

### UC-RUNAS-D01 - proposed new: Get completed help as the configured operator
- Actors: Operator, Agent Helper, worker. Preconditions: Approved root policy and authenticated target CLI.
- Basic flow: Operator submits ordinary helper prompt without overrides; helper resolves Grok and sharpninja; generic worker verifies UID; answer and cleanup correlated.
- Alternative/exception flows: Unavailable worker, identity mismatch, incomplete answer or echo: fail without local fallback.
- Postcondition: Completed actual answer and verified cleanup, MCP identity unchanged.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-HELP-011. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC1, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC2, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC4, FR-MCP-HELP-011/AC1.
- TDD P1/P2: Helper_DefaultsOnly_CompletedRealBody, HelperReceiptCorrelation_Required. Real verification P4/P5.

### UC-RUNAS-D02 - proposed new: Explicitly select a different strategy without default leakage
- Actors: Operator, caller, strategy resolver. Preconditions: Registered strategy and permitted local/profile execution.
- Basic flow: Select Codex or another existing strategy; scoped defaults resolve; same selected implementation executes.
- Alternative/exception flows: Unknown alias/config duplicate or unsupported crossUID capability/policy: named failure, not Grok replacement.
- Postcondition: Selected identity/path/model and semantics retained.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001, FR-MCP-HELP-011, FR-MCP-RUNAS-002. AC references: FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001/AC1, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001/AC2, FR-MCP-HELP-011/AC2, FR-MCP-RUNAS-002/AC1.
- TDD P1: Helper_CodexOverride_DoesNotInheritGrokExecutable, SelectedStrategyNeverReplaced. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D03 - proposed new: Execute supported callers with workspace/admin identity
- Actors: Operator, TODO, voice, triage, pool, requirements, workspace-policy. Preconditions: Per-request workspace context and approved profile.
- Basic flow: Resolve operation workspace, preserve null/empty semantics and explicit admin fallback, invoke generic selected strategy.
- Alternative/exception flows: Active denied feature blocks rollout absent named approval; no public UID override or wrong-account retry.
- Postcondition: All matrix callers either execute desired UID or explicitly fail before launch.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC1, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001/AC3, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001/AC4.
- TDD P1: TodoDeployedGrokSelection_Preserved, TodoAdminRunAs_AfterOverwriteRemoval, CallerRunAsRequirements_DelegatesSelectedOneShot, CallerRunAsWorkspacePolicy_DelegatesSelectedOneShot. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D04 - proposed new: Use full delegated conversation and cancel safely
- Actors: Operator, remote session adapter, selected strategy. Preconditions: Established authenticated session.
- Basic flow: Read/stream initial response, send/stream subsequent prompt, escape/end/dispose; preserve batch/interactive result/PID.
- Alternative/exception flows: Concurrent op Busy; cancellation/disconnect closes descendants; no resume or prompt replay.
- Postcondition: Correct result semantics and session cleanup receipt.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-002, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-002/AC2, FR-MCP-RUNAS-002/AC3, FR-MCP-RUNAS-002/AC4, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC5.
- TDD P2: RemoteSessionContractTests_AllMembers, CancelCompletion_FirstTerminalWins, EndDispose_IdempotentWaitsCleanup, StreamAbandonment_ClosesSession. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D05 - proposed new: Reject unauthorized or malformed delegated launch
- Actors: Unauthorized peer, MCP caller, root policy. Preconditions: Restricted socket and readable immutable policy.
- Basic flow: Authorized peer submits allowed framed request; validate schema/profile/runtime before launch.
- Alternative/exception flows: Wrong peer, injected identity/env/secret, malformed/oversize/replayed frame or mutable path rejected without value leakage.
- Postcondition: No unauthorized launch, safe typed failure and preserved audit.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-RUNAS-003. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC3, FR-MCP-RUNAS-003/AC3.
- TDD P2: PeerRejectedBeforeParse, PolicyMismatch_NoLaunch, DelegatedSecrets_DeniedWithoutValueLeak, PublicCallerLaneOverride_Rejected. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D06 - proposed new: Recover worker and descendant resources after failure
- Actors: Worker supervisor, operator, systemd. Preconditions: Persisted registry and running invocation/session units.
- Basic flow: Record launch before submission; on exit/crash stop all registered units, capture receipts, drain/read/delete, restart admission only after proof.
- Alternative/exception flows: Manager unavailable or cleanup unknown: unhealthy and retain resources, operator recovery required.
- Postcondition: No leaked descendant/files or false cleanup success.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-RUNAS-003. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC5, FR-MCP-RUNAS-003/AC3.
- TDD P2: WorkerCrash_RegistrySweepBeforeAdmission, RegistrySiblingUnitsAllStopped, FailedUnitsResetAfterReceipt, CleanupFailed_BlocksAdmission. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D07 - proposed new: Admit help while general work is busy
- Actors: Operator, helper, voice, TODO, broker lanes. Preconditions: Named approval of general-lane blocking and configured deadlines.
- Basic flow: General voice holds its slot; helper uses reserved slot independently.
- Alternative/exception flows: Second helper/general gets immediate Busy; open voice blocks general TODO/requirements/parser up to approved hard limit.
- Postcondition: At most two CLI invocations, helper not starved, release only after cleanup.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-003. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-003/AC1, FR-MCP-RUNAS-003/AC2.
- TDD P2: HelperWhileVoiceOpen_Admitted, SameLaneSecond_Busy, GeneralLane_VoiceOpen_TodoBusy, GeneralLane_VoiceOpen_RequirementsAndPolicyBusy. Real verification P4.

### UC-RUNAS-D08 - proposed new: Deploy or roll back a verified release using Nuke
- Actors: Administrator, Nuke, fixed installer, services. Preconditions: Known prerequisite schema/host release, approved source/test/artifact digest, administrator auth.
- Basic flow: Unprivileged Nuke builds tested bundle, fixed elevation locks journal, backs up, verifies worker then MCP, merges approved configuration, verifies real goal.
- Alternative/exception flows: Any transition/crash resumes or rolls back exact known state; unsafe recovery stops admission/services, retains evidence.
- Postcondition: Accepted verified release or verified old-state restore, no data/schema mutation.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001. AC references: FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001/platform, FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001/preserve, FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001/lifecycle, FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001/validation, FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC6, FR-MCP-GROKDEFAULTS-001/AC5.
- TDD P3: NukeUpdateService_InvokesFixedPkexecAfterValidatedPackage, TransitionRestartAndFailureRollback, ConfigACLPreserved, RecoveryFailed_AdmissionStopped. Real verification P4/P5.

### UC-RUNAS-D09 - proposed new: Review major-phase evidence without per-increment HV
- Actors: Operator, developer, Claude reviewer. Preconditions: Every increment evidence retained and major phase complete.
- Basic flow: Developer validates mocks then real red/green/refactor and full regressions per increment; completed phase provides immutable scope and full evidence to Claude.
- Alternative/exception flows: Missing AC/test/UC link, skipped/failed/empty suite, incomplete receipts/audit or sub98 verdict blocks next phase.
- Postcondition: Major-phase review complete with >=98 scores and durable full verdict/readback, no HV inside increments.
- Realizes: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001, FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001. AC references: FR-MCP-RUNAS-001/AC7, FR-MCP-SERVICEUPDATE-001/validation.
- TDD P3: GateValidator_RejectsMissingMockRedGreenEvidence, HvScheduler_OnlyCompletedMajorPhase, AuditReceipt_RequiresFullVerdictAndReadback. Real verification P1/P2/P3/P4/P5.
## 13. Major phases, strict TDD coverage and HV cadence (operator directive)
Planning closure P0: complete exact plan/catalog/architecture decisions, then planning HV iteration until technical agreement. This is the previously requested plan review, NOT per-increment development review. Formal full durable reviewer JSONL/audit/readback and explicit operator architecture/Act approval remain prerequisites. I0 executes provenance/worktree/canonical capture/baseline after approval; required readbacks/manifest review are local procedural checks, not an extra development HV launch. Incomplete plan/prerequisite phase cannot grant permission for product code.
P1 - Selection, shared strategies and identity routing (I1,I2,I3). Owns settings, deployed-key compatibility, public/common contract extraction, generic identity decoration, caller guard/error semantics and helper-result acceptance harness. Exit: all P1 AC TDD complete and full current/prior unit scopes zero failures/skips, no fake PID acceptance; then exactly one Claude phase-end review covering AC/tests/diff/receipts. No HV between I1/I2/I3 or at mock gate.
P2 - Transport, verified process lifecycle and secure worker (I4,I5,I6). Owns every wire/session member, registry and pipe contracts, cgroup cleanup, policy/socket/runtime/env and admission lanes. Exit: all P2 mock/red/green/refactor evidence and full unit regression complete, then one Claude phase-end review. No HV inside I4/I5/I6; no unpaid/paid integration result used to replace unit evidence.
P3 - Deployment implementation and current-line forward-port (I7,I8). Owns Nuke installer/rollback/config metadata, evidence gate validator, mappings/current source names. Exit: all P3 TDD plus full unit suite on actual integrated SHA and validated immutable artifact/test catalog; then one Claude phase-end review. Missing formal reviewer audit still blocks next phase even if numerical scores high.
P4 - Human-guided integration and isolated staging. Only starts after ALL unit AC gates across codebase pass and P3 review agrees. Implement integration tests with mocks/fault fixtures first where contract testable, real red/green then actual separate-user/socket/systemd/runtime proofs. Any newly discovered product defect gets approved AC amendment and its named unit mock/red/green increment before integration rerun. Complete ALL required integration/jobs/runtime closure/auth/tooling/rollback probes and staging defaults-only helper acceptance; then one Claude phase-end review of integrated artifact and readiness. No HV on partial staging runs. P4 AGREE plus explicit administrator deployment approval required before production.
P5 - Approved production transaction and final acceptance. Deploy exact P4 tested/approved artifact via Nuke fixed elevation only, run real defaults-only answer/UID/hardening/cleanup/data integrity tests. Complete production acceptance first, then one Claude final phase-end review; no midtransaction HV. Done only P5 review scores >=98, zero unresolved FAIL/acceptance-blocking UNKNOWN, durable complete evidence and audit readback.
Failed phase-end review: remediate findings with same strict incremental mock-first TDD/full regressions; rerun HV ONLY once the WHOLE revised major phase is complete, no review per finding/test. Phase boundaries may not be subdivided to defeat this schedule. Normal code/test inspection, prerequisite audits, unit/integration tests and self-validation are not HV; they still occur at every increment. Test mocks passing before real code is never waived by reduced HV frequency.
Coverage ledger: exact record/AC ID -> operation(new/update) -> UC draft/canonical ID -> P/I -> absolute test project/class/method -> mock success+deliberate wrong assertion proof -> same-assertion real red/green/refactor -> full regression manifest/TRX -> final actual proof -> review gate. Rows referencing many cases expand per theory data case so no identity/caller/timeout/security edge hidden in vague umbrella test. AC with multi-increment ownership must have coverage in each assigned increment. Add exact project paths when W test manifest is created; before product code, ledger rejects missing/unowned AC, unlinked UC, missing test discovery, nonexistent methods, changed assertion hashes, fake runtime proof, missing platform scope, or future skipped placeholders. EVERY section0-10 normative obligation must reference catalog AC(s); newly discovered unmapped clause blocks implementation until approved catalog amendment. Validate FR<->TR<->TEST and UC Realizes round-trip with canonical plugin readback, not just local text. Snapshot preexisting unaffected AC too; preserve all old meanings unless named supersession approved.
Administrative obligations (e.g. worktree isolation, provenance, approval, canonical persistence, test/audit gates) use I0 signed/checksummed inspection evidence plus P3 GateValidator TDD, not fictional behavior-changing red for already-existing Git/plugin operations. Real-world AC still requires real final proof. For all TR and TEST criteria use their own scoped AC rows even when text mirrors FR; no requirement marked complete until its mapped real verification passed.

Implementation Plan (Detailed)

Phase 0 - Requirements alignment and traceability
1) Update FR/TR docs to introduce pooled-agent runtime requirements and adjust existing voice/agent requirements for unified pool behavior.
2) Add/adjust mappings in TR-per-FR-Mapping.md and add/adjust test requirements in Testing-Requirements.md.
3) Update Requirements-Matrix.md to reflect new planned/implemented status.

Phase 1 - Configuration contracts
1) Add appsettings-bound pool configuration model (collection of agents) with fields: AgentName, AgentPath, AgentModel, AgentSeed, AgentParameters.
2) Add validation: AgentName unique (case-insensitive), AgentPath required, AgentModel default fallback, AgentParameters optional key/value payload.
3) Define one-shot input DTO contract with mutually-exclusive prompt mode:
   - promptTemplateId (+ optional values dictionary/context options)
   - promptText (ad-hoc)
   Validation: exactly one mode required.
4) Add template variable merge rule: caller values override workspace-context-derived values on key collision.

Phase 2 - Agent pool runtime service
1) Create IAgentPoolService + implementation as singleton runtime coordinator.
2) Maintain in-memory registry per pooled agent:
   - lifecycle (offline/starting/idle/busy/stopping/error)
   - current sessionId
   - active work descriptor (voice/one-shot)
   - lastRequestPrompt snapshot
   - active voice link count
   - read-only subscriber count
3) Launch all pooled agents through voice interactive session mechanism only.
4) Implement lifecycle controls: start, stop, immediate recycle (terminate current work and restart).

Phase 3 - One-shot queue orchestration
1) Add FIFO queue manager with persisted in-memory job model (queued/processing/completed/failed/canceled).
2) Dispatch queued one-shot jobs to next eligible idle pooled agent.
3) Implement queue operations:
   - list queue state
   - enqueue (TODO-derived and free-form)
   - cancel (queued and in-flight)
   - remove queued item
   - move up/down (queued items only; processing item immutable)
4) Capture job timeline and agent assignment metadata for UI/SSE.

Phase 4 - Prompt template resolution endpoint
1) Add endpoint to accept promptTemplateId + values dictionary (+ optional workspace-context expansion).
2) Resolve template via template service/renderer and return rendered prompt text.
3) Return validation errors for unknown template, missing required vars, or invalid mode combinations.
4) Reuse endpoint from Director and one-shot enqueue flows to normalize rendering behavior.

Phase 5 - Server API surface
1) Add pooled-agent availability endpoint(s) exposing live status for each configured agent.
2) Add pooled-agent control endpoint(s): connect voice, stop, start, recycle-now.
3) Add queue management endpoint(s) including free-form one-shot enqueue.
4) Add notification SSE endpoint (separate monitor stream) with JSON payload:
   - AgentName
   - LastRequestPrompt
   - SessionId
   plus lifecycle status and timestamp.
5) Add read-only response stream endpoint allowing multiple concurrent subscribers.

Phase 6 - Voice and one-shot integration
1) Refactor voice session creation to support AgentName targeting and linking to already-running pooled agents (including agents processing one-shot).
2) Refactor TODO one-shot flows to submit to queue instead of auto-streaming immediate process output.
3) Notify requester when one-shot transitions to processing; allow user to attach via voice or read-only stream.

Phase 7 - Director Agent Pool tab
1) Add Agent Pool tab data model and refresh loop backed by pooled availability + queue endpoints.
2) Implement agent actions: connect voice, recycle-now, stop, start.
3) Add queue panel actions: cancel/remove, move up/down, free-form enqueue.
4) Add notification monitor pane consuming dedicated SSE stream.
5) Add template-driven enqueue path using prompt resolve endpoint.

Phase 8 - Testing and verification
1) Add server tests for configuration validation, pool lifecycle transitions, queue dispatch/cancel/reorder semantics, and template input-mode validation.
2) Add SSE tests for lifecycle event ordering/payload schema.
3) Add voice integration tests for AgentName attach-to-busy behavior.
4) Add Director tests for Agent Pool tab action wiring and queue interaction behaviors.
5) Run targeted build/tests for touched projects and verify no regressions.

Phase 9 - Delivery and documentation closure
1) Requirements docs alignment target IDs: FR-MCP-028/046 revisions, FR-MCP-052/053/054/055/056/057/058, and TR-MCP-AGENT-004/005, TR-MCP-API-002/003, TR-MCP-TPL-006, TR-MCP-VOICE-004, TR-MCP-DIR-004.
2) Keep session log entries synchronized with decisions/actions/files.
3) Publish final implementation summary and residual risks (backpressure, prompt privacy, recycle semantics).

Execution Breakdown (File-Level / API-Level)
A) Options + validation - Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Options/AgentPoolOptions.cs:
  * AgentPoolOptions.SectionName = "AgentPool"
  * Agents: List<AgentPoolDefinitionOptions>
- Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Options/AgentPoolDefinitionOptions.cs fields:
  * AgentName, AgentPath, AgentModel, AgentSeed, AgentParameters
  * IsInteractiveDefault, IsTodoPlanDefault, IsTodoStatusDefault, IsTodoImplementDefault
- Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Options/AgentPoolOptionsValidator.cs:
  * Validate unique AgentName (case-insensitive)
  * Validate required AgentPath and AgentName
  * Validate max one default per intent flag
- Wire in Program.cs:
  * Configure<AgentPoolOptions>(section)
  * AddSingleton<IValidateOptions<AgentPoolOptions>, AgentPoolOptionsValidator>()

B) Voice runtime extensions - Extend VoiceSessionCreateRequest:
  * AgentName (optional)
  * OneShotSession (optional; internal behavioral flag)
- Extend IVoiceConversationService with:
  * TryGetOrCreateNamedSessionAsync(agentName,...)
  * SendSessionMessageAsync(sessionId,message,...)
- Update VoiceConversationService state:
  * Track AgentName + IsOneShotSession
  * Allow named session reuse for pooled agents
  * Send message to interactive session for presence signaling
- Update VoiceController:
  * CreateSession supports AgentName attach path
  * turn/stream sends "User is here." after stream open (interactive only)
  * turn/stream sends "User is AFK." on disconnect/cancel (interactive only)

C) Agent Pool runtime + queue - Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Services/IAgentPoolService.cs - Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Services/AgentPoolService.cs:
  * Agent registry state (lifecycle/session/last prompt/active links/subscribers)
  * Queue state store (queued/processing/completed/failed/canceled)
  * Queue operations (enqueue/list/cancel/remove/reorder)
  * Dispatcher loop selecting idle eligible agent
  * Intent-default fallback routing when AgentName omitted
  * Notification stream fan-out for lifecycle events
  * Read-only job stream fan-out for multi-subscriber consumption
- Register AgentPoolService singleton in Program.cs
D) One-shot contract + prompt resolution - Add one-shot request/response DTOs:
  * Context enum: Plan, Status, Implement, AdHoc
  * AgentName optional, promptTemplateId optional, promptText optional, id optional
  * Values dictionary optional, UseWorkspaceContext flag optional
- Validation rules:
  * Reject both promptTemplateId + promptText
  * Require resolvable prompt source
  * Require id when template-resolved (explicit or context-template path)
  * Require ad-hoc prompt when context=AdHoc and no template id
- Prompt resolution behavior:
  * explicit template id -> render via template renderer/service
  * no template id + context Plan/Status/Implement -> existing context-template flow
  * merge values: workspace/context defaults first, caller values overwrite conflicts
  * inject id into variables for {id} substitution

E) Controllers / endpoints - Add src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Controllers/AgentPoolController.cs:
  * GET /mcpserver/agent-pool/agents
  * POST /mcpserver/agent-pool/agents/{agentName}/start

  * POST /mcpserver/agent-pool/agents/{agentName}/recycle

  * GET /mcpserver/agent-pool/queue

  * POST /mcpserver/agent-pool/queue/{jobId}/cancel

  * POST /mcpserver/agent-pool/queue/{jobId}/move-up
  * POST /mcpserver/agent-pool/queue/{jobId}/move-down
  * GET /mcpserver/agent-pool/notifications (SSE)
  * GET /mcpserver/agent-pool/jobs/{jobId}/stream (SSE)
- Extend PromptTemplateController:
  * POST /mcpserver/templates/{id}/resolve
  * input: values dictionary
  * output: populated rendered prompt

F) TODO one-shot integration - Add optional enqueue endpoints for TODO plan/status/implement that use agent pool queue - Preserve existing SSE prompt routes for compatibility while enabling queued model
G) Tests and verification - Add tests:
  * AgentPoolOptions validator tests
  * AgentPoolService queue lifecycle + reorder/cancel tests
  * Intent-default routing tests
  * Prompt resolve endpoint tests
  * Voice presence signal tests for AFK/here behavior (interactive vs one-shot)
- Build + test commands:

description: Audit the entire codebase to ensure every data source follows the Single Source of Truth principle.

description: Observed 2026-10-11 (Linux, node 26.8.2, plugins/core/lib-node jest, receipt scratchpad bug-plugincore-001-green.log): the full lib-node suite is 134 passed, 3 failed; all three failures are tests/workspace.test.ts workspace_ensure cases. The same three fail with HEAD's sources (lib-node-workspace-at-head.log), so they predate BUG-PLUGINCORE-001; P0.1 had not run the lib-node jest suite before.

Failure (O): "registers and initializes a missing untrusted workspace" expects created true, trusted false, markerReloadRequired true, workspacePath "F:\\GitHub\\NewWorkspace", and receives created false, trusted true, workspacePath /home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/.claude/worktrees/session-20261009 (the worktree whose marker sits above the test's working directory). Inference to verify: the drive-letter path is not absolute on Linux, so workspace_ensure falls back to marker discovery and reports the current workspace instead of the requested one. If that fallback is product behavior it may also be a product defect (a request for one workspace silently acting on another); the root-cause step decides.

Root cause (2026-10-11): test portability. handleWorkspaceTool resolves workspacePath with path.resolve (src/tools/workspace.ts:110-116); on Linux the drive-letter literal is relative and lands under the jest working directory (plugins/core/lib-node), and fullBootstrap's findMarkerFile walks up (src/discovery/marker-resolver.ts:22-31) to the worktree's marker, so the tool reports that workspace as trusted. On Windows the literal is absolute with no marker above it. Fix (commit 450fe07c, test-only): unmarkedWorkspacePath(name), a uniquely named absolute path under os.tmpdir() with no marker above it. RED: full lib-node suite 134 passed, 3 failed (these three; same with HEAD sources, lib-node-workspace-at-head.log). GREEN (bug-baseline-018-green.log): 15 suites, 137 passed, 0 failed. Product behavior noted for the operator, not changed: workspace_ensure resolves a non-absolute workspacePath against the process directory before marker discovery, although its description asks for an absolute root.

description: Failing tests: RequirementsDocumentServiceTests (6), RequirementsWikiExportOrchestratorTests (4), RequirementsWikiExportConfigTests GenerateWikiAsync cases (3), WikiDumpG6OverlayTests (3), RequirementsDatabaseDocumentServiceTests (3), RequirementsTwelfthAdversarialReviewTests (2), HandoffD3D5OverlayTests (1), DocsSyncG8OverlayTests.G8_GenerateWikiAsync_Default_WritesWikiFoldersWithoutDump (1): 23 tests.

Errors: System.IO.DirectoryNotFoundException: Atomic Linux export-root capture could not find '/tmp/<test-root>/...' at QBrainAi.Client.LinuxPhysicalPathResolver.OpenDirectoryNoCrossDevice (src/QBrainAi.Client/LinuxPhysicalPathResolver.cs:260); DirectoryNotFoundException from WorkspaceContainedFileSystem.OpenLinuxPathBeneathRoot for nested paths (wiki/github, wiki-output/azure); NotSupportedException "Linux requirements export cleanup rejects nested stale paths before mutation because the kernel lacks a contained atomic delete" (RequirementsDocumentExportWriter.DeleteStaleFilesAsync).

Hypothesis (unverified): The export root is resolved with RESOLVE_NO_XDEV from an anchor above /tmp, so the tmpfs mount crossing is reported as "could not find"; nested directories are opened without being created first.
Triage: triage-report-b9f345e7ace7420a8aa2761f1fcac3e9.

Found by the P0.1 unit baseline of PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001 on 2026-10-10 (Linux omarchy host, SDK 10.0.201, worktree .claude/worktrees/session-20261009; application code identical to the approval HEAD 5a2dd88d, only build/ and tests/Build.Tests changed since): G2 ./build.ps1 Test ran QBrainAi.Support.Mcp.Tests (Failed 63, Passed 2893, Skipped 0) and stopped there (fail-fast without --test-run-id); the other unit projects ran with the Test target's exact settings (only QBrainAi.McpAgent.Tests failed: 8 of 65). Unit total: Failed 71, Passed 4271, Skipped 0. Host note: /tmp is a separate tmpfs mount (st_dev 57; / is btrfs, st_dev 31), so every Path.GetTempPath() test root crosses a mount from /.

PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001 P0.1: every failure or skip in the G2 baseline predates the plan, is filed in triage, and must be fixed under its own TODO before slice A1 starts (zero failures, zero skips, no exclusion list).

Fix by Byrd v4: root cause with evidence (confirm or refute the hypothesis), the failing tests as the recorded RED (or a corrected RED if a test encodes the wrong behavior), the fix, every affected project green with zero skips, then a Codex gpt-6-sol xhigh HV before done.

Root cause (2026-10-10; refutes the tmpfs/RESOLVE_NO_XDEV hypothesis: tmpfs is an approved mount and capture anchors at the mount that contains the path, so /tmp is not the cause): a deliberate Windows/Linux asymmetry in contained export I/O (src/QBrainAi.Storage/WorkspaceContainedFileSystem.ExportRoot.cs). On Windows, OpenWindowsExportRoot calls Directory.CreateDirectory(rootPath) and EnsureWindowsDirectory creates nested folders through the root handle. On Linux, OpenLinuxExportRoot requires the export root to exist, and EnsureLinuxDirectoryRooted (WorkspaceContainedFileSystem.BoundedTraversal.cs:263) requires every nested folder to exist; its comment states that "a Linux export may use only directories that already resolve under the pinned root" because a validate-then-mkdirat sequence could let a moved parent receive the new directory outside the root. Stale-file cleanup is likewise refused on Linux (RequirementsDocumentExportWriter.DeleteStaleFilesAsync: "the kernel lacks a contained atomic delete"). The tests run exports into fresh temporary workspaces, so on Linux: 18 fail because the export root does not exist (for example docs/Project/wiki), 2 because a nested folder does not exist (wiki/github, wiki-output), 1 because stale cleanup is refused, and the 2 RequirementsTwelfthAdversarialReviewTests alias-swap races surface EEXIST and DirectoryNotFoundException, which their accepted-failure list does not include. Product impact: on Linux, a requirements or wiki export into a folder that does not exist yet fails. Fix direction needs an operator decision: (a) create the export root and nested folders on Linux too (parity with Windows: create the root before capture, create nested folders with mkdirat on a pinned parent descriptor and verify the new folder's identity through the root before use), and delete stale files with unlinkat on a pinned parent; or (b) keep the strict Linux design and make the tests pre-create folders and expect the refusals on Linux, leaving fresh-folder exports unsupported there.

Operator decision (2026-10-11T00:02:53Z): "Create folders on Linux (Recommended)": parity with Windows; create the export root before capture, nested folders with mkdirat on a pinned parent plus identity verification, stale cleanup with unlinkat on a pinned parent; planned and HV'd as a product change.

Plan drafted (2026-10-11): docs/plans/PLAN-LINUXEXPORTCREATE-001.md, commit 93746b9b. D1 pinned-parent mkdirat with statx no-follow identity verification through the anchor and rollback of only the created, still-empty inode (EEXIST accepted only after verification, never removed); D2 nested folders through D1; D3 export root creation before capture (unbounded-mount policy first, deepest existing ancestor pinned, identity compare with the capture); D4 nested stale deletion through a pinned, re-verified parent. Accountability TR-MCP-USECASE-017 (3 ACs planned). Six new Linux native tests planned. Codex gpt-6-sol xhigh plan-readiness HV r1 launched; implementation waits for AGREE.

Plan HV round 1 (Codex gpt-6-sol xhigh, docs/receipts/hv/hostile-validator-linuxexportcreate-r1-20261011T115738Z.md): DISAGREE 84/72, 1 PASS, 7 FAIL, 1 UNKNOWN; F1 operator decision, F2-F7 implementer edits. Operator decision (2026-10-11T12:32:55Z, AskUserQuestion, verbatim label): "Accept stated residuals (Recommended)": keep the pinned-parent design, state the create race (R1) and delete race (R2) as accepted residual risk, narrow deletion by renaming to a random name in the same pinned directory and verifying the inode before unlinking, and add adversarial tests for both. Plan revision 2 answers F1-F7 (section 9); TODO linked to TR-MCP-USECASE-017 and FR-MCP-USECASE-015 (F5).

Operator decision (2026-10-11T12:58:57Z, verbatim): "Implement landlock with failback." after HV round 2 (DISAGREE 87/82; moved-ancestor and moved-parent effects beyond R1/R2) and my answer that Linux has no ACID filesystem transactions but enforces path-beneath confinement through the Landlock LSM (active here: /sys/kernel/security/lsm lists landlock; kernel 7.2.5). Contract: every Linux nested create/delete and missing-root creation runs on a dedicated thread confined by Landlock to the pinned root (or, for a missing root, the pinned deepest existing ancestor), so a moved parent makes mkdirat/unlinkat fail with EACCES and nothing outside is touched; where Landlock is unavailable the code falls back to today's fail-closed refusal. The R1/R2 residual design and name-narrowed removal are superseded. Implementation is test-first; the plan document is revised as the design record and reviewed with the implementation in the batched HV.

Implemented and committed 8009289c (2026-10-11): Landlock-confined creation and nested deletion with fail-closed fallback (plan revision 3). Two more root causes found and fixed: the requirements export writer refused nested stale paths on Linux regardless (now WorkspaceExportRoot.SupportsNestedDeletion), and the Linux traversal threw for a not-yet-created export directory where Windows returns empty (parity for a missing start directory only). Also docs/wiki.yaml still named docs/McpServer-UseCase-Extension-Design-v3.0.md, renamed by 6de989f3 (fixed through the YAML object-mutation helper, CRLF kept). GREEN (bug-baseline-001-green2.log): 126 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped. Root cause (2026-10-10, refines the hypothesis): two parts. (1) RepoFileService (1 test): NormalizeRelative trims leading slashes before the rooted check (src/QBrainAi.Services/Services/RepoFileService.cs:260-264, then IsPathTraversal at :285), so on Linux "/tmp/repo_external_<id>/outside.txt" becomes the repo-relative "tmp/repo_external_<id>/outside.txt" and resolves to <root>/tmp/...; it stays inside the root (no escape, the outside file is never read or written), but an absolute path is silently reinterpreted, and a write would create the file inside the repository. On Windows "C:\..." stays rooted and is rejected. The leading-slash trim may exist so clients can send "/src/x.cs" as repo-relative; on Unix that convention cannot be told apart from an absolute path, so the fix direction needs an operator decision on the path contract. (2) SessionLogSessionAttrTests (3 tests): Windows-shaped test data (WorkspacePath "E:\tests\sessionlog-session-attr", ForeignPluginPath "Q:\__mcp_unit_test__\...") is relative on Linux, so the foreign path lands inside the workspace; SessionLogWorkspaceAttributionValidator itself checks Path.IsPathRooted without trimming (lines 139-161) and is correct, so this part belongs to the BUG-BASELINE-002 cluster. Root cause (2026-10-10, confirms the hypothesis; both are test assertions of Windows-only platform behavior). (1) HandoffContainedFileReaderTests.ReadAsync_OpenShare_BlocksWritesAndDeletes never calls the product reader: it opens its own FileStream with FileShare.Read (line 81) and asserts that the OS blocks a writer (line 82) and File.Delete (line 83). Windows enforces share modes; on Linux they are advisory and unlink never fails on an open file. Its requirement ("P1-6 / P2-1: the reader opens with a share mode that blocks writes and deletes") is Windows-centric; the per-OS refinement is an AC: on Windows writes and deletes are blocked while the reader holds the file, on Linux the held descriptor keeps reading the original bytes after a concurrent delete. (2) CodexCliAgentExecutionStrategyTests.ReadInitialResponseAsync_UsesCodexExecWithoutCopilotInteractiveFlags asserts the cmd.exe-escaped form model_reasoning_effort=\"xhigh\" on every OS (line 60), but only the Windows launch goes through cmd.exe /c; on Linux the product passes the TOML literal model_reasoning_effort="xhigh" (CodexCliAgentExecutionStrategy.HighestReasoningEffortConfig) as one argv element, which is correct for codex -c. The test already branches on OS for FileName; the quoting assertion needs the same branch.

Root cause (2026-10-11, read-only analysis; O = observed with receipt, I = inference). Shared causes: C1 product (O): ResolveSymlinksOnApprovedMounts probes each prefix with File.GetAttributes (src/QBrainAi.Client/LinuxPhysicalPathResolver.cs:394, :421), which on Unix follows a symlink with stat(), so preflight enters an alias target on a FUSE mount before the mount table rejects it, against the BoundedFileSystemPolicy.cs:3-7 contract that preflight never traverses userspace mounts. C2 product (O): SqliteBoundedConnectionOpener.OpenIsolatedAsync runs that preflight synchronously before its first await (SqliteBoundedConnectionOpener.cs:62 then :373), so no WaitAsync or worker bound applies. C3 fixture: the delayed-FUSE helper runs single-threaded (-s, BugTriage139SixteenthLinuxTests.cs:679) (O), so one unanswered request from another process (I: most likely gvfsd-trash probing .Trash on new mounts) wedges even the root GETATTR. C4 (O): no [Fact(Timeout)] in the project, no blame-hang in Build.Test.cs, fs.fuse request timeouts 0. C5 (O): the test user is uid 1000, CapEff 0; setuid /usr/bin/mount refuses bind mounts for non-root; the same class asserts non-root (BugTriage139EighteenthLinuxTests.cs:23-28, :693); unprivileged user namespaces are enabled (unprivileged_userns_clone=1, no AppArmor). C6 (O): /tmp is tmpfs, / and /home are separate btrfs subvolumes.

Per test: (1) SqliteOpen_SafeSymlinkIntoFuse hung 48 m: C1 on the caller thread (C2) blocked on the wedged helper (C3); product wrong; fix C1 by reading links with readlink (FileInfo.LinkTarget) and probing existence with the existing TryStatxPath (AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW). (2) SqliteOpen_AliasReplacementAtNativeOpen: the worker's OpenFileNoCrossDevice (LinuxPhysicalPathResolver.cs:150) hits the same follow; the worker bound fired (TimeoutException); product wrong (C1). (3) WorkspaceIdentityFourteenthNativeTests.NativeResolver_RepeatedPlatformCallsLeaveNoActiveWorkers: an absolute alias from the /tmp tmpfs to / (btrfs) gives EXDEV under the anchored RESOLVE_NO_XDEV; SQLite and data-file opens pre-resolve this case (LinuxPhysicalPathResolver.cs:324-329, SqliteBoundedConnectionOpener.cs:365-369) but identity resolution (WorkspaceIdentityPath.cs:292) does not; product wrong (absolute aliases under /home would fail the same way); fix by routing identity resolution through the corrected resolver. (4-6) the three RequirementsExport delayed-FUSE replacement cases fail at mount --bind (exit 32, C5) before reaching product code. (7) RootReplacedBeforeAuthorityCapture is a cascade of the failed bind (product correct). (8) BugTriage139EighteenthTraversalTests.BlockingMetadata asserts a Windows-only rename block on the pinned root (line 60; Linux descriptors never block rename); per-OS assertion like BUG-BASELINE-004; a faithful Linux "root stays pinned" check would expose a product defect: the root descriptor is disposed at the public timeout (BoundedTraversal.cs:99, ExportRoot.cs:536) while the worker still uses it through DangerousGetHandle without AddRef (ExportRoot.cs:554, BoundedTraversal.cs:883).

Fix direction: product fixes for C1, C2, and identity resolution (bug fixes, no requirement change) test-first; test hardening (drop the helper's -s, a watchdog that kills the helper on cancellation, and [Fact(Timeout)]); for cases 4-7 either a test-only change (mount a second helper directly at the destination through unprivileged fusermount3; the TEST-MCP-USECASE-020 ACs say delayed mount, not bind mount) or running them under unshare --user --map-root-user --mount (a Nuke change, as in the 2026-09-16 C10 run that passed 5/5); operator decisions: that approach, the timeout value, and whether to fix the root-descriptor AddRef defect now. History (O): the tests arrived in 55fae924 (2026-09-16); no receipt shows cases 3-8 passing as a plain non-root user; a leftover /tmp/mcp-sixteenth-fuse-2f4b5fd800d749319bf99c408244aa95 (2026-10-09 17:06) remains from an earlier hang.

Operator decision (2026-10-11T00:49:59Z): "Test-only fusermount3 (Recommended)": mount a second copy of the delayed helper directly at the destination through unprivileged fusermount3 for cases 4-7; drop the helper's -s, add a cancellation watchdog and per-test timeouts; the three product fixes (preflight following symlinks, synchronous preflight, identity resolution across mounts) proceed test-first.

Done (2026-10-11, uncommitted at this write, commit follows). Operator decisions 2026-10-11: "Fix it now (Recommended)" for the root-descriptor AddRef defect and "Keep 60 s (Recommended)" for the per-test timeouts. Fixture (test-only): the delayed-FUSE helper runs multi-threaded (no -s); replacement roots are second helper instances mounted through unprivileged fusermount3 (MountDelayedFuseAtAsync replaces the root-only mount --bind); a watchdog kills every helper on the test token or after 30 s; teardown detaches with fusermount3 -u -z ignoring the test token; ten FUSE tests carry [Fact(Timeout = 60_000)]. Root cause observed live on 2026-10-10 at 22:14Z (Linux, SDK 10.0.201) during the BUG-BUILD-006 trim-inventory run: the Build.Tests process (PID 2575389, 0 s CPU over 850 s, no child processes) was blocked on EOF of a dotnet child that had already exited; the other ends of both redirected pipes (pipe:[16191191] stdout, pipe:[16191192] stderr) were held as fd 1 and fd 2 by an MSBuild worker node (MSBuild.dll /nodemode:1 /nodeReuse:true, PID 2575659) that the child's build had spawned and that had been reparented to the user systemd (PPID 1082); the node also held the test process's stdin. Node reuse keeps such a node alive after the build, so EOF never arrives; when an idle reusable node already exists the build connects to it instead and nothing inherits the pipes, which explains the earlier passing run. TrimAnalysisWarningInventoryTests bounds only WaitForExitAsync (20 minutes); the await of its output tasks that follows is unbounded. Receipt: bug-build-007-evidence.log.txt.

Call sites with an unbounded wait on redirected child output (6, not 3): MigrationAssemblyObsoleteWarningTests.RunDotnetBuildAsync (dotnet build; the observed suite hang), TrimAnalysisWarningInventoryTests.RunDotnetAsync (dotnet build and publish; exit bounded at 20 minutes, output unbounded; hung live), RequirementsWikiPublishScriptTests.RunScriptAsync (pwsh; reads stdout to the end before stderr, which can also deadlock on a full stderr pipe), YamlObjectMutationTests.RunPowerShellAsync (pwsh), ServiceUpdateTests.Native and the ServiceUpdateTests fixture tar runner (exit bounded at 30 s, then an unbounded Task.WaitAll on the output).

Refined 2026-10-10 after HV round 1 (finding F-B7) by three bounded experiments; receipts in docs/receipts/_bug-build-003-009-20261010T224959Z/ (bug-build-007-evidence-note.md and bug-build-007-experiment1..3.log.txt). The live log's elapsed times were read about five minutes apart, so they do not show the node predating the test. Provenance: in every experiment the node's parent PID, read while the build child ran, was the child. Mechanism: dotnet test sets MSBUILDENSURESTDOUTFORTASKPROCESSES=1 for vstest.console, the test host, and the test executable (the dotnet test process itself has it unset), so every build a Build.Tests case starts inherits it. With it set, MSBuild starts worker nodes without redirecting their standard streams, and a node spawned by the build inherits the build's redirected stdout and stderr (the output stayed open 30 s after exit). Without it, as from a plain shell, the node gets its own streams and the output closes at once. Node reuse keeps the node alive after the build. When an idle node with a matching handshake exists, the build reuses it and spawns nothing, so the hang is intermittent. With --disable-build-servers the node exits with the build and the output closes at once, even with the variable set.

description: Receipt: scratchpad sync-agent-plugins.log (to be committed with the BUG-BUILD-008 receipts). ./build.ps1 SyncAgentPlugins --agent-plugin-parent /home/sharpninja/github, 2026-10-11T03:36:44Z-03:37:18Z, exit 255. It synced the core and wrappers into the staged plugin and all 8 plugin repos (each integrity check "core integrity OK: 14 files match"), ran npm ci and npm run build in plugins/core/lib-node, then threw at Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:554: "npm pack produced 'qbrainai-qbrain-ai-plugin-core-0.2.0.tgz' but plugins/core/lib-node/package.json declares version 0.2.0 (expected 'sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core-0.2.0.tgz')." Vendor refresh, version bump, and cache refresh did not run.

Root cause (O): commit 6de989f3 (2026-10-05, "Rename the product root to QBrainAi and keep 1.x aliases.") renamed plugins/core/lib-node from @sharpninja/mcpserver-plugin-core to @qbrainai/qbrain-ai-plugin-core; npm pack names its tarball from the package name and version (leading @ dropped, / replaced by -), but RefreshNodePluginCoreVendorPackages builds the expected name from a hardcoded prefix (Build.SyncAgentPlugins.cs:551, $"sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core-{manifestVersion}.tgz"), so every run since the rename stops here. TR-MCP-SYNC-001 asks for a version guard ("assert that npm pack produced a tarball whose embedded version matches plugins/core/lib-node/package.json"); the prefix is not part of that contract. The stable vendor file name sharpninja-mcpserver-plugin-core.tgz and the consumer reference rewrite stay as TR-MCP-SYNC-001 specifies.

Fix direction (bug fix, no requirement change; strengthen TR-MCP-SYNC-001 with an AC): derive the expected packed file name from package.json name and version by npm's naming rule, test-first in Build.Tests (RED: the current source builds the name from the hardcoded prefix; a renamed manifest must yield the npm name). Accountable through TR only (operator ruling); TR-MCP-SYNC-001 currently maps to FR-MCP-143, which the ruling "NUKE is only accountable through TR" places under FR-MCP-BUILD-001 instead; note for PLAN-BUILDWHATIF-001.

Coupled decision (BUG-PLUGINCORE-001): with this fixed, the target would vendor the renamed core into cline, cline-v2, and opencode, and the renamed core no longer exports createMcpServerPluginCore, which cline-v2 and opencode import.

technicalDetails: MCP proxy routes are server endpoints, not Android-side rewrites. The server must forward device authorization and token polling requests to Keycloak using configured OIDC authority/realm endpoints.
Preserve OIDC response payloads/status codes so Android device-flow polling logic continues to work unchanged except for base URL (:7147 instead of :7080).
Route examples: GET /auth/config (local metadata), POST /auth/device (proxy to Keycloak device authorization endpoint), POST /auth/token (proxy to Keycloak token endpoint).
items.note: Android can reach MCP server on :7147 but may not be able to reach Keycloak directly on :7080. Add MCP-hosted OIDC proxy routes so Android device-flow traffic stays on :7147.
description: Expose MCP-server OIDC proxy routes for Android app use: GET /auth/config, POST /auth/device, and POST /auth/token.
Android app should call MCP on :7147 only; MCP server forwards OIDC requests to Keycloak (:7080) and returns equivalent responses.
This fixes the current failure mode where /auth/config succeeds on :7147 but token polling later fails when Android tries to connect directly to Keycloak on :7080.

items.title: Create mcpserver Claude Code Plugin
technicalDetails: 13 files + 1 gitignore update across 6 phases.

Plugin follows Claude Code plugin format: .claude-plugin/plugin.json manifest, .mcp.json (FLAT format) for MCP server connections, hooks/hooks.json for lifecycle hooks, skills/name/SKILL.md for slash commands and model-invoked skills, agents/name.md for custom agents.
Valid hook events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit. SessionStart does NOT exist.
Hook entry fields: type (command), command (string, supports ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}), timeout (int seconds). No shell field.
User-invoked skills identified by argument-hint presence, not a user_invoked field.
Agent frontmatter supports: name, description, tools (comma-separated), model (sonnet/haiku/opus/inherit), color.
plugin.json valid fields: name, description, version, author (name/email). No homepage.
.mcp.json flat format: { server-name: { type: http, url: ... } }. No mcpServers wrapper.
Uses pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive for all PowerShell.
Full plan at .claude/plans/flickering-cooking-finch.md
description: Create a Claude Code plugin at .claude/plugins/mcpserver/ that automates MCP server session bootstrapping and provides skills for common workflows.
Connects Claude Code to 45 MCP tools via Streamable HTTP at /mcp-transport (no API key needed).
Provides bootstrap hook for automatic health verification and context injection.
User-invoked skills: /mcpserver:status, /mcpserver:todo, /mcpserver:deploy, /mcpserver:tunnel.
Model-invoked skills: session logging workflow, TODO workflow, requirements tracking.
Custom agent: mcp-context-researcher for context search and GraphRAG research.
## Implementation Phases
### Phase 1: Core Infrastructure (3 files)
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json - Plugin manifest (fields: name, description, version, author with name/email). No homepage field.
- .mcp.json - MCP transport connection. FLAT format: { server-name: { type: http, url: ... } }. No mcpServers wrapper.
- README.md - Plugin documentation
### Phase 2: Session Bootstrap (2 files) - REVISED
- hooks/hooks.json - Hook registration. Top-level has description + hooks object. Valid events: PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, UserPromptSubmit. SessionStart does NOT exist.
- hooks/hooks-handlers/session-start.ps1 - Bootstrap script. Reads AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml, verifies /health with nonce, injects context or MCP_UNTRUSTED warning.

- DESIGN DECISION NEEDED: Use UserPromptSubmit hook (fires on first prompt, auto-bootstrap) OR create a /mcpserver:start user-invoked skill for explicit bootstrap. UserPromptSubmit fires on EVERY prompt so script must be idempotent and fast (check cached state).
- Hook entry fields: type, command, timeout ONLY. No shell field. Use $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT for paths.
### Phase 3: User-Invoked Skills (4 files)
- skills/status/SKILL.md - /mcpserver:status. Frontmatter: name, description, argument-hint, allowed-tools: [Bash, Read]
- skills/todo/SKILL.md - /mcpserver:todo. Frontmatter: name, description, argument-hint, allowed-tools: [Bash, Read]
- skills/deploy/SKILL.md - /mcpserver:deploy. Frontmatter: name, description, argument-hint, allowed-tools: [Bash, Read]
- skills/tunnel/SKILL.md - /mcpserver:tunnel. Frontmatter: name, description, argument-hint, allowed-tools: [Bash, Read]
- NOTE: User-invoked is determined by presence of argument-hint field. No user_invoked: true field exists.
### Phase 4: Model-Invoked Skills (3 files)
- skills/mcp-session-logging/SKILL.md - Only name + description in frontmatter. No argument-hint = model-invoked.
- skills/mcp-todo-workflow/SKILL.md - TODO CRUD, ID format rules, GitHub sync behavior
- skills/mcp-requirements/SKILL.md - FR/TR/TEST format, docs/Project/ locations
### Phase 5: Custom Agent (1 file)
- agents/mcp-context-researcher.md - Frontmatter must include: name, description, tools (comma-separated), model (sonnet), color (cyan)
### Phase 6: Housekeeping (1 task)
- Update .gitignore with .claude/*.local.md and .claude/*.local.json patterns
## Key Design Decisions
- .mcp.json uses FLAT format with localhost:7147/mcp-transport (no API key, portable)
- Bootstrap hook uses UserPromptSubmit (not SessionStart which does not exist). Script must be idempotent.
- Hook commands reference plugin root via ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} variable, not hardcoded paths
- Model-invoked skills provide naming conventions and workflow guides
- API key included in hook context output for REST API fallback calls
## Audit Corrections Applied (2026-04-06)
- CRITICAL: SessionStart is not a valid hook event. Changed to UserPromptSubmit or explicit /mcpserver:start skill.
- CRITICAL: shell field does not exist in hook entries. Removed.
- CRITICAL: .mcp.json must use flat format, not mcpServers wrapper.
- MODERATE: user_invoked: true is not a valid field. Use argument-hint presence instead.
- MODERATE: homepage is not a valid plugin.json field. Removed.
- MODERATE: Added allowed-tools to all user-invoked skills.
- MODERATE: Added model, color, tools fields to agent definition.
- MINOR: Added .gitignore task for plugin local config files.
- MINOR: Use ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in hook commands instead of hardcoded paths.
- MINOR: Added top-level description field to hooks.json spec.
## Verification
1. Bootstrap hook fires on first prompt and injects MCP server context
2. /mcpserver:status shows health, workspace, tunnel status
3. /mcpserver:todo lists TODOs via MCP tools
4. mcp-session-logging skill activates when logging turns
5. mcp-todo-workflow skill activates with correct naming conventions
6. All 45 MCP tools visible in Claude tool list
items.note: Audited 2026-04-06. 3 critical corrections (SessionStart invalid, shell field invalid, mcp.json format), 4 moderate (user_invoked field, homepage, allowed-tools, agent fields), 3 minor (gitignore, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, hooks.json description).

description:
Operator directive (2026-10-06): all persisted paths should use forward slashes, since Windows accepts '/' as a separator. Canonical rule: persist '/' separators everywhere; keep the case-sensitivity tag in storage keys (windows: case-insensitive vs case-sensitive:); detect Windows-origin paths by drive letter ('C:/') or UNC ('//server/share') rather than by separator. Preserve the UNC leading '//' (must not collapse to '/server/share'). Convert back to '\' only at OS boundaries that require it (\\?\ long-path prefixes, cmd.exe arguments, some external tools).

Motivation (observed 2026-10-06, LocalProxy PAYTON-LEGION2 on Windows -> hub LAB-OMARCHY on Linux):
1. Triage intake on the Linux hub stored originalWorkspacePath='/opt/mcpserver/app/C:\Users\kingd' (Windows absolute path resolved as Linux-relative to the working directory); triage_status by the proxy's own workspacePath returned not_found. Triage report triage-report-b7ff17da715f4cc485dcac8b001c47ce, group triage-group-bfc69ceba9e9f1fb. Note: separator normalization alone does not fix this; 'C:/Users/kingd' is still not rooted on Linux (Path.IsPathRooted=false), so drive-letter/UNC rooting detection is required.
2. CORRECTED 2026-10-06: todo_list with workspacePath='F:\GitHub\McpServer' through the LocalProxy returned 0 items because the hub held no TODOs for that workspace (no proxy->hub data backfill on enrollment; 1062 local TODOs vs 0 on hub under the proxy's workspace ids), NOT because of path mapping. It is therefore not evidence for this path-normalization work. Tracked separately: triage-report-692d92ea13a44d48aaf5d66019e4cbef, group triage-group-18acf2d8a0adfecd.
3. Related federation drift (TodoPath, CurrentRequirementLayerKey not synced to hub canonical Workspaces rows): triage-report-cac6e7077ba64edcb32de97d2532176f, group triage-group-d708a0e30a2b7195.

Relevant code: src/McpServer.Client/WorkspaceIdentityPath.cs (NormalizePath, BuildStorageKey, DetectPlatform), src/McpServer.Storage/WorkspaceIdentity.cs, src/McpServer.Services/Services/FederationTopologyService.cs (UpsertWorkspaceAsync, CreateGlobalWorkspaceId), triage intake controller/service.

Constraints: storage-key/hash changes affect existing Workspaces, FederationWorkspaces (GlobalWorkspaceId = SHA256(lower(proxyId:windows:UPPER(path)))), and every workspace-scoped table; requires a migration across SQLite, SQL Server and PostgreSQL providers and a re-enrollment/re-hash plan for federated proxies. Follow the Byrd Development Process: requirements (FR/TR) and red tests first (Windows drive, UNC, mixed separators, Linux absolute, Linux hub receiving Windows paths, round-trip to OS boundary), mocks, then implementation; full suite green.

items.title: [DONE] Seed Agent Pool per workspace/definition and enforce workspace-correct session routing
technicalDetails: Audit baseline: verified existing composite runtime key in AgentPoolService (`AgentInstanceKey(agentName, workspacePath)`), startup host registration for AgentPoolSeedService in Program.cs, workspace-aware queue dispatch, and workspace-aware DTOs/controller wiring.
Gap A (voice isolation): VoiceConversationService.CreateSessionAsync reused idle sessions by agent name only; this allowed cross-workspace reuse for same agent definition.

Gap B (device identity collision): AgentPoolService.StartAgentAsync generated device IDs from workspace folder name only (`Path.GetFileName(workspace)`), allowing collisions across distinct workspaces with identical folder names.
Gap C (request override): AgentPoolController accepted caller-provided workspacePath in one-shot enqueue/resolve payloads, enabling workspace override instead of strict context-bound routing.

Remediation A: VoiceConversationService now reuses pooled sessions only when both agent name and workspace path match (case-insensitive), preserving same-workspace reuse while preventing cross-workspace bleed-through.

Remediation B: AgentPoolService now builds pooled device IDs using a deterministic SHA-256 hash of normalized workspace path (`agent-pool-{agent}@{workspaceHash}`), eliminating cross-workspace device collisions.
Remediation C: AgentPoolController now enforces workspace from WorkspaceContext for queue/resolve operations and agent runtime listing (ignores query/payload workspace overrides).
Validation scope includes unit coverage additions for startup seed behavior and controller workspace enforcement, plus updated voice-session reuse tests to prove workspace isolation semantics.
description: On startup, the Agent Pool should automatically seed a running agent instance for every (workspace × agent definition) combination. When an SSE or MCP session connects, route it to the agent instance that is bound to the correct workspace, ensuring workspace isolation. This prevents agents from operating against the wrong workspace context and eliminates the need for manual agent provisioning.

technicalDetails: ARCHITECTURE: In-process fan-out pub/sub via ChannelChangeEventBus (bounded channel, 1000-item buffer, drop-oldest). SSE delivery via EventStreamController at GET /mcpserver/events?category=xxx. Per-subscriber channels ensure independent consumption.
DI REGISTRATION: builder.Services.AddSingleton<IChangeEventBus, ChannelChangeEventBus>() in Program.cs - MUST be singleton so all scoped services and the SSE controller share the same bus instance.

PUBLISH LOCATION: Service layer (not controllers) for all CRUD operations so internal callers (IssueTodoSyncService, RequirementsService.AnalyzeAsync) also emit events. Controller-only for operations that bypass services (GitHubController gh cli calls, workspace start/stop side effects).

UPSERT DETECTION: For upsert methods (SessionLogService.SubmitAsync, AgentService.UpsertDefinitionAsync/UpsertWorkspaceAgentAsync), detect create vs update by checking if entity existed before write, then emit appropriate ChangeEventActions.Created or .Updated.
NEW CATEGORIES: Add 'agent' and 'requirements' to ChangeEventCategories.cs. These are needed for AgentService (8 mutations) and RequirementsDocumentService (11 mutations).

CONSTRUCTOR INJECTION PATTERN: Add IChangeEventBus parameter to service constructors. For TodoService which has 2 constructors (DI + internal test), add to both. For services using primary constructors (like RequirementsService), add parameter to the primary constructor.
FR-MCP-031 FIX: EventStreamController.cs line 8 incorrectly references FR-MCP-031 (McpServer Management Web UI). Change to FR-MCP-045 (new Workspace Change Notifications FR).

FIRE-AND-FORGET: PublishAsync is synchronous (writes to all subscriber channels via TryWrite), so no need for try/catch or background queueing. However, wrap in try/catch with LogWarning for defensive coding per TR-MCP-LOG-001.
RESOURCE URI CONVENTION: mcp://workspace/{category}/{entityId} - e.g. mcp://workspace/todo/MVP-MCP-001, mcp://workspace/sessionlog/Copilot/session-123, mcp://workspace/gh/issues/42.

TEST STRATEGY: (1) ChannelChangeEventBusTests - publish/subscribe fan-out, buffer overflow drop-oldest, cancellation, multiple subscribers. (2) Per-service tests verifying PublishAsync is called with correct category/action/entityId after each mutation - use NSubstitute mock of IChangeEventBus. (3) EventStreamController integration test via CustomWebApplicationFactory - register bus, publish event, verify SSE output.

'/' }, OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) and returns the challenge result. Accepts optional 'returnUrl' query param and validates it is local. Add @page '/login' directive.

Task A3 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/Login.cshtml.cs: LoginModel : PageModel. Inject nothing beyond PageModel. OnGet(string? returnUrl) validates returnUrl is a local URL (Url.IsLocalUrl), constructs AuthenticationProperties with RedirectUri, returns Challenge(properties, OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme). No Blazor component - must be a pure Razor Page.

Task A4 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/Logout.cshtml: non-interactive Razor Page. PageModel.OnGet() calls HttpContext.SignOutAsync(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) then HttpContext.SignOutAsync(OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, new AuthenticationProperties { RedirectUri = '/' }). This triggers the provider end_session redirect if configured. Add @page '/logout' directive.

Task A5 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/Logout.cshtml.cs: LogoutModel : PageModel. OnGetAsync() calls await HttpContext.SignOutAsync(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) then returns await HttpContext.SignOutAsync(OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme, new AuthenticationProperties { RedirectUri = '/' }). Both schemes must be signed out.

Task A6 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/AccessDenied.razor: standard Blazor @page '/access-denied' component. Shows PrimerBlankslate with Heading='Access Denied' Description='You do not have permission to view this page.' and a link back to /dashboard. No [Authorize] on this page itself (it must be accessible without auth). No code-behind needed.

Task B1 - Update src/McpServer.Web/Routes.razor: change <RouteView RouteData='@routeData' DefaultLayout='@typeof(MainLayout)' /> to <AuthorizeRouteView RouteData='@routeData' DefaultLayout='@typeof(MainLayout)'><NotAuthorized><RedirectToLogin /></NotAuthorized></AuthorizeRouteView>. The NotAuthorized block should differentiate: if context.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated == true redirect to /access-denied else redirect to /login with returnUrl.

Task B2 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Components/Auth/RedirectToLogin.razor: a parameter-less component that on OnInitializedAsync calls NavigationManager.NavigateTo('/login?returnUrl=' + Uri.EscapeDataString(NavigationManager.Uri), forceLoad: true). This is required because NavigateTo from inside AuthorizeRouteView must force a full page load to allow the non-circuit Razor Page to execute.

Task C1 - Update src/McpServer.Web/Components/Layout/MainLayout.razor: add <AuthorizeView> block at the top of the shell. In <Authorized> show context.User.Identity?.Name (falling back to 'name' claim) and a link to /logout. In <NotAuthorized> show a login link to /login. Add the new auth header above the <aside>/<main> app-shell structure using Primer CSS d-flex/flex-items-center/Header patterns.

Task C2 - Update src/McpServer.Web/Components/Layout/NavMenu.razor: add @inject AuthenticationStateProvider AuthStateProvider. Wrap admin-only nav sections (e.g. Auth Config, future admin areas) in <AuthorizeView Roles='admin'> to hide them from non-admin users. Add a top-level user display name and logout link at the bottom of the sidebar using Primer CSS.

Task D1 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Authorization/WebRoleContext.cs: public sealed class WebRoleContext : IRoleContext. Inject IHttpContextAccessor. IsAuthenticated returns _accessor.HttpContext?.User.Identity?.IsAuthenticated ?? false. Roles returns (_accessor.HttpContext?.User.Claims.Where(c => c.Type == 'role').Select(c => c.Value) ?? []).ToList(). HasRole(string role) uses case-insensitive Contains on Roles list. Add XML doc comments.

Task D2 - Update src/McpServer.Web/WebServiceRegistration.cs: add services.AddHttpContextAccessor() and services.TryAddSingleton<IRoleContext, WebRoleContext>() BEFORE the call to services.AddUiCore(). This ensures the real WebRoleContext wins over AllowAllRoleContext from the TryAdd fallback inside AddUiCore. Import McpServer.Web.Authorization and McpServer.UI.Core.Authorization namespaces.

Task E1 - Create src/McpServer.Web/Authorization/BearerTokenAccessor.cs: internal sealed class BearerTokenAccessor. Inject IHttpContextAccessor. Method: Task<string?> GetAccessTokenAsync(CancellationToken ct) calls await _accessor.HttpContext.GetTokenAsync('access_token') returning null when not authenticated. This isolates the token retrieval from WebMcpContext.

Task E2 - Update src/McpServer.Web/WebMcpContext.cs: inject BearerTokenAccessor. In EnsureInitializedAsync, before the API key check, try var bearerToken = await _bearerTokenAccessor.GetAccessTokenAsync(cancellationToken). If non-null/non-whitespace, set client.BearerToken = bearerToken and return (skip InitializeAsync). The existing EnsureInitializedAsync early return for non-empty BearerToken already handles the short-circuit correctly.

Task E3 - Update src/McpServer.Web/appsettings.json: add McpServer section at root level: { 'McpServer': { 'BaseUrl': 'http://localhost:7147', 'ApiKey': '', 'WorkspacePath': '' } }. These are development defaults. Production overrides go in environment variables or appsettings.Production.json.

Task E4 - Create src/McpServer.Web/appsettings.Development.json: override Authentication:Schemes:OpenIdConnect:Authority with 'http://localhost:7080/realms/mcp', ClientId with 'mcp-web', and Authentication:Authorization:RequireAuthenticatedUserByDefault with true. This makes dev require login by default while prod stays false until explicitly configured.

Task F1 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/McpServer.Web.Tests.csproj: net9.0 class library targeting McpServer.Web. Add PackageReferences for: Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Testing (for WebApplicationFactory), xunit, xunit.runner.visualstudio, coverlet.collector, Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk. Add ProjectReference to src/McpServer.Web/McpServer.Web.csproj.

Task F2 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/Auth/LoginPageTests.cs: WebApplicationFactory<Program> test. Test: GET /login returns 302 redirect to OIDC authority (or challenges). Mock the OIDC handler or use TestAuthHandler to simulate the challenge. Verify IActionResult is a ChallengeResult or that Location header points to OIDC authority. Use builder.ConfigureServices() to stub the OIDC metadata.

Task F3 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/Auth/LogoutPageTests.cs: WebApplicationFactory test. Test: GET /logout when authenticated returns 302 to OIDC provider's end_session endpoint or to /. Verify cookie is cleared (response does not include auth cookie or sets it to empty). Use TestAuthHandler to pre-authenticate the request.
Task F4 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/Auth/AccessDeniedPageTests.cs: verify GET /access-denied returns 200 and the page contains 'Access Denied' heading without requiring authentication.

Task F5 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/Auth/AuthorizeRouteViewTests.cs: Bunit or WebApplicationFactory test. Verify that a page with [Authorize] attribute redirects unauthenticated users to /login and allows authenticated users through. Use TestAuthHandler with pre-seeded ClaimsPrincipal.

Task F6 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/Authorization/WebRoleContextTests.cs: unit tests. Test IsAuthenticated returns false when IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext is null. Test IsAuthenticated returns true when HttpContext.User.Identity.IsAuthenticated is true. Test Roles enumerates 'role' typed claims from HttpContext.User. Test HasRole('admin') returns true/false correctly with case-insensitive comparison.

Task F7 - Create tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/WebMcpContextTests.cs: unit tests. Test EnsureInitializedAsync sets client.BearerToken when BearerTokenAccessor returns a non-empty token. Test EnsureInitializedAsync calls InitializeAsync when no token is available. Use fake IConfiguration and mock BearerTokenAccessor.

Task G1 - Build verification: run 'dotnet build src/McpServer.Web -c Debug' and 'dotnet build tests/McpServer.Web.Tests -c Debug'. Fix all compilation errors introduced by the new auth pages, WebRoleContext, BearerTokenAccessor, and updated WebMcpContext. Verify no CA/nullable warnings become errors.
Task G2 - Test verification: run 'dotnet test tests/McpServer.Web.Tests -c Debug'. All new tests must pass. Fix any test failures.

items.title: Web UI OIDC integration - full login/logout flow, AuthorizeRouteView, RoleContext, token forwarding, and tests
technicalDetails: DONE - Program.cs: AddAuthentication().AddCookie().AddOpenIdConnect() fully config-driven from Authentication:Schemes section. UseAuthentication() and UseAuthorization() in pipeline. AddCascadingAuthenticationState() registered. Authorization policies (AgentManager/Admin) driven from Authentication:Authorization:Policies.

DONE - appsettings.json: full Authentication section with Cookie (CookieName/LoginPath/LogoutPath/AccessDeniedPath), OpenIdConnect (Authority/ClientId/ClientSecret/ResponseType/CallbackPath/SignedOutCallbackPath/MapInboundClaims/GetClaimsFromUserInfoEndpoint/ClaimMapping/Scope), Authorization (RequireAuthenticatedUserByDefault:false, Policies).
DONE - Pages/Auth/AuthConfig.razor: read-only display of server OIDC config via AuthConfigViewModel. NavMenu links to /auth/config.
DONE - _Imports.razor: imports Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.Authorization and Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authorization. CascadingAuthenticationState is registered and cascades to all components.
DONE - WebServiceRegistration.cs: IAuthConfigApiClient scoped. AddUiCore() fallback registers AllowAllRoleContext and AllowAllAuthorizationPolicyService.

MISSING - Login flow: CookieAuthenticationDefaults.LoginPath=/login but no page exists. Must be a non-interactive Razor Page (not Blazor component) because HttpContext.ChallengeAsync() requires a non-circuit HTTP context. File: src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/Login.cshtml + Login.cshtml.cs. Must add AddRazorPages() + MapRazorPages() to Program.cs.

MISSING - Logout flow: CookieAuthenticationDefaults.LogoutPath=/logout but no page exists. Razor Page that calls HttpContext.SignOutAsync(CookieAuthenticationDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) then HttpContext.SignOutAsync(OpenIdConnectDefaults.AuthenticationScheme) to trigger provider end_session redirect. File: src/McpServer.Web/Pages/Auth/Logout.cshtml + Logout.cshtml.cs.

MISSING - AccessDenied page: AccessDeniedPath=/access-denied but no page exists. A simple Blazor component page (Pages/Auth/AccessDenied.razor) with Primer CSS styling and a link back to dashboard. No HttpContext needed.

MISSING - Routes.razor: Uses RouteView which ignores [Authorize] attributes. Must switch to AuthorizeRouteView with a NotAuthorized block that redirects to /login for unauthenticated users and shows access-denied for authenticated-but-unauthorized users.

MISSING - User identity display: MainLayout.razor and NavMenu.razor have no user identity section. Need an AuthorizeView-based header/nav block showing the logged-in username (from context.User.Identity.Name or 'name' claim) and a logout link when authenticated, plus a login link when anonymous.

MISSING - WebRoleContext: ServiceCollectionExtensions.AddUiCore() defaults to AllowAllRoleContext. McpServer.Web must register a concrete WebRoleContext : IRoleContext that reads from IHttpContextAccessor.HttpContext.User (IsAuthenticated, ClaimsPrincipal.IsInRole). File: src/McpServer.Web/Authorization/WebRoleContext.cs. Register before AddUiCore() in WebServiceRegistration.cs via services.AddHttpContextAccessor() + services.TryAddSingleton<IRoleContext, WebRoleContext>().

MISSING - WebMcpContext token forwarding: EnsureInitializedAsync currently auto-discovers API key via client.InitializeAsync(). When a user is authenticated, their OIDC access_token (saved via options.SaveTokens=true) should be forwarded as Bearer token to the McpServer API. Inject IHttpContextAccessor, call HttpContext.GetTokenAsync('access_token') on each scoped request, and set client.BearerToken. The BearerToken check in EnsureInitializedAsync already short-circuits initialization if a bearer token is set.

MISSING - appsettings.json McpServer section: WebMcpContext reads McpServer:BaseUrl, McpServer:ApiKey, McpServer:WorkspacePath from IConfiguration but appsettings.json has no McpServer section. Add defaults: BaseUrl=http://localhost:7147, ApiKey=(empty), WorkspacePath=(empty).
MISSING - appsettings.Development.json: Create with Authority overriding to http://localhost:7080/realms/mcp (Keycloak dev), ClientId=mcp-web, and RequireAuthenticatedUserByDefault=true for dev.

MISSING - McpServer.Web.Tests: tests/McpServer.Web.Tests/ directory is empty. McpServer.Web.Tests.csproj exists per commit history but has no content. Need WebApplicationFactory-based or Bunit-based tests covering: Login challenge redirect, Logout sign-out, AccessDenied rendering, AuthorizeRouteView blocking, WebRoleContext claim reading, bearer token forwarding.
Build verification: dotnet build src/McpServer.Web -c Debug. Test verification: dotnet test tests/McpServer.Web.Tests -c Debug. Must fix all compilation errors before marking done.

Keycloak integration context: Keycloak is on :7080, MCP API on :7147, MCP Web (Blazor) on :7100 or similar separate port. OIDC proxy routes (/auth/config, /auth/device, /auth/token) on the MCP API server are for Android/device-flow clients, not the web browser flow. Web UI uses standard browser-based Authorization Code flow (PKCE optional, code response type already configured).

Role claim mapping: MapInboundClaims=false, RoleClaimType='role' (per appsettings.json ClaimMapping). Keycloak emits realm roles as 'realm_access.roles' by default. An OnTokenValidated event handler may be needed to flatten realm_access.roles into individual 'role' claims - or configure Keycloak client to include roles as flat claims. This is a Keycloak client mapper configuration concern, but must be tested.
description: Web UI needs a complete OIDC authentication integration: login challenge, logout, access-denied, AuthorizeRouteView, user identity display in nav, WebRoleContext wired to ClaimsPrincipal, bearer token forwarding from the Blazor session to the McpServer API, and end-to-end tests.

AUDIT STATUS (2026-03-05): OIDC middleware is registered in Program.cs and appsettings.json has all required config fields with placeholder values. The following are MISSING and block auth from working: Login page, Logout endpoint, AccessDenied page, AuthorizeRouteView in Routes.razor, user identity display, WebRoleContext, bearer token forwarding, McpServer config section, and Web.Tests content.

The McpServer.Web project already has AuthConfig display (read-only), Primer CSS layout, all feature pages (Todos/Sessions/Templates/Context/Health/Agents/Workspaces), SSE subscription, and adapter infrastructure. This TODO covers only the remaining auth wiring.
items.note: AUDIT (2026-03-05): McpServer.Web has the OIDC middleware wired in Program.cs (AddAuthentication/AddCookie/AddOpenIdConnect, UseAuthentication/UseAuthorization, AddCascadingAuthenticationState), a correct appsettings.json Authentication section, the AuthConfig read-only display page (Phase 3.1/Phase 5), and service registrations. However the following are MISSING and must be built: (1) Login/Logout/AccessDenied pages (app cannot authenticate at all without these -- requests to /login/logout 404), (2) Routes.razor AuthorizeRouteView upgrade (Authorize attributes are currently ignored), (3) User identity header in MainLayout/NavMenu, (4) WebRoleContext connecting ClaimsPrincipal roles to IAuthorizationPolicyService, (5) WebMcpContext access-token forwarding to the McpServer API, (6) McpServer section in appsettings.json, (7) McpServer.Web.Tests tests. FR-MCP-031 is the primary requirement.

items.title: [READY] Complete Director MVVM/CQRS endpoint coverage with per-area ViewModels, handlers, commands, and RBAC tab visibility
technicalDetails: Scope: all /mcpserver/* areas plus /auth/config and /health diagnostics/event views. ACTUAL endpoint count is 112 REST endpoints (not the originally estimated ~78). Excludes minimal-API endpoints (pairing, server-startup-utc, etc.) and MCP protocol tools.
Handler granularity: strict 1:1 endpoint-to-handler mapping (query/command + handler + ViewModel async command).
ViewModel convention: per area ListViewModel + DetailViewModel pair. Both inherit from AreaListViewModelBase<T> or AreaDetailViewModelBase<T>.
Director shell must consume ViewModels only for migrated tabs; use McpServer.Client adapters behind UI.Core service abstractions.
RBAC source: JWT realm roles parsed by Director auth (realm_roles/roles). Role tiers: viewer, agent-manager, admin. Already implemented via DirectorRoleContext + DirectorAuthorizationPolicyService.
RBAC UX behavior: hide unauthorized tabs and commands; still rely on server-side auth as authority. Already enforced in MainScreen.RebuildTabs().
UI.Core existing infrastructure: IRoleContext, IAuthorizationPolicyService, McpArea (17 areas), McpActionKeys (27 keys), McpRoles (3 tiers), AllowAll* defaults, AreaList/DetailViewModelBase.
Area API abstractions: 10 of 14 exist. Missing: IAgentApiClient, IToolRegistryApiClient, IGitHubApiClient, IEventStreamApiClient.
McpServer.Client gaps: AgentClient (14 methods), RequirementsClient (20 methods), VoiceClient (6 methods), EventStreamClient (1 SSE method) = 41 missing client methods.

CQRS infrastructure: McpServer.Cqrs provides IDispatcher, IQueryHandler<TQuery,TResult>, ICommandHandler<TCommand,TResult>. McpServer.Cqrs.Mvvm provides CqrsRelayCommand, ViewModelCommandAttribute, IViewModelRegistry.
Testing gap: McpServer.UI.Core has ZERO dedicated tests. Need new test project with handler tests, ViewModel tests, authorization policy tests.
Director screens: 9 of 10 use ViewModels. AgentScreen is the sole outlier (uses AgentScreenHandler with direct HTTP calls).
Approximate endpoint coverage target revised from ~78 to 112 based on actual controller audit.
description: Implement complete MCP Director administration coverage through the McpServer.UI.Core MVVM/CQRS layer.
