items.title: Migrate all templates to YAML files
technicalDetails: TEMPLATE FILE FORMAT: Each YAML file contains named template strings. The YAML structure varies by category: marker prompt is a single multi-line string under a key, TODO prompts are 3 named strings, pairing pages are 3 named strings. Use YAML block scalars (|) for multi-line template content to preserve formatting.

MARKER PROMPT TEMPLATE FILE (templates/default-marker-prompt.hbs.yaml): Structure: { template: | ... 570 lines of Handlebars ... }. Loaded by MarkerFileService at startup. Falls back to embedded resource or inline constant if file not found (graceful degradation). Handlebars placeholders: {{baseUrl}}, {{apiKey}}, {{workspace.*}}, {{#if}}/{{#each}} blocks for ban lists. File preserves exact Handlebars syntax - no conversion needed.

TODO PROMPT TEMPLATE FILE (templates/todo-prompts.yaml): Structure: { statusPrompt: |, implementPrompt: |, planPrompt: | }. Loaded by TodoPromptService via IOptionsMonitor<TodoPromptOptions>. Placeholder syntax: {id}, {title}, {baseUrl} - simple string.Replace, not Handlebars. Existing Mcp:TodoPrompts config section overrides file values (config > file > default).

PAIRING HTML TEMPLATE FILE (templates/pairing-pages.yaml): Structure: { loginPage: |, keyPage: |, notConfiguredPage: | }. Loaded by PairingHtml static class (refactored to instance with DI). HTML uses C# string interpolation - template file contains raw HTML with {0}, {1} placeholder tokens for String.Format or named {{variable}} tokens for simple replacement.

TEMPLATE LOADING SERVICE: Create ITemplateLoader interface with LoadAsync<T>(string templateName, CancellationToken ct) -> T. Implementation TemplateFileLoader reads from Mcp:TemplatePath directory using YamlDotNet deserialization. Registered as singleton in DI. Caches loaded templates in ConcurrentDictionary. Supports hot-reload via FileSystemWatcher (optional, behind config flag).

FALLBACK STRATEGY: If template file does not exist, fall back to embedded constant (existing DefaultPromptTemplate, TodoPromptDefaults, PairingHtml inline strings). Log warning on fallback. This ensures zero-config startup still works and existing deployments are not broken.

CONFIGURATION: New appsettings.json section Mcp:Templates: { BasePath: "templates", EnableHotReload: false, EnableFileSystemWatcher: false }. BasePath resolved relative to content root. Empty or missing BasePath means use embedded defaults.

TESTING: Unit tests verify: (1) TemplateFileLoader reads and deserializes YAML correctly, (2) fallback to embedded defaults when file missing, (3) MarkerFileService uses loaded template instead of const, (4) TodoPromptService uses loaded templates, (5) config override precedence: appsettings > file > embedded default.
description: Externalize all inline template strings from C# source code into loadable YAML files, enabling runtime customization without recompilation.
MarkerFileService.DefaultPromptTemplate (570 lines of Handlebars) is the primary migration target - move to templates/default-marker-prompt.hbs.yaml.
TodoPromptDefaults (3 templates: StatusPrompt, ImplementPrompt, PlanPrompt) - move to templates/todo-prompts.yaml.
PairingHtml (3 HTML pages: LoginPage, KeyPage, NotConfiguredPage) - move to templates/pairing-pages.yaml.

Template rendering engines (HandlebarsDotNet for marker, string.Replace for TODO prompts, C# interpolation for HTML) remain in code. Only the template content source changes from const string to file-loaded string.

Configuration: Mcp:TemplatePath setting specifies base directory for template files (default: templates/ relative to content root). Templates loaded at startup and cached. IOptionsMonitor for hot-reload support.

items.title: Implement per-agent workspace functionality
technicalDetails: AGENT PROCESS MANAGER: Create IAgentProcessManager interface with methods: LaunchAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct) -> AgentProcessInfo, StopAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct) -> bool, GetStatusAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct) -> AgentProcessInfo, ListRunningAsync(workspacePath?, ct) -> IReadOnlyList<AgentProcessInfo>. Implementation AgentProcessManager uses System.Diagnostics.Process to launch agent CLI tools. Tracks running processes in ConcurrentDictionary<(string workspacePath, string agentId), AgentProcessInfo>. AgentProcessInfo record: ProcessId, AgentId, WorkspacePath, StartedAt, Status (Running/Stopped/Failed), ExitCode?, WorkDirectory (isolated path if applicable).

LAUNCH COMMAND RESOLUTION: When launching an agent, resolve the effective launch command: AgentWorkspaceEntity.LaunchCommandOverride ?? AgentDefinitionEntity.LaunchCommand. Support command template variables: {workspacePath}, {agentId}, {branchName}, {modelList}, {seedPrompt}. Parse command string into executable + arguments. Log resolved command to AgentEventLog with EventType=Launch.

ISOLATION STRATEGY: Create IAgentIsolationStrategy interface with PrepareWorkDirectoryAsync(workspacePath, agentId, isolationMode, ct) -> string (returns working directory path) and CleanupAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct). Implementations: (1) NoneIsolationStrategy - returns workspacePath as-is. (2) WorktreeIsolationStrategy - runs git worktree add .agents/{agentId} -b agent/{agentId}/{timestamp} from workspacePath, returns worktree path. (3) CloneIsolationStrategy - runs git clone --depth 1 --single-branch workspacePath .agents/{agentId}-clone, returns clone path. Register via strategy pattern in DI. AgentWorkspaceEntity.AgentIsolation field (worktree/clone/null) selects strategy.

WORKTREE LIFECYCLE: WorktreeIsolationStrategy.PrepareWorkDirectoryAsync: (1) Create .agents/ directory under workspace root if not exists. (2) Run git worktree add .agents/{agentId} -b agent/{agentId}/{yyyyMMdd-HHmmss}. (3) Copy/symlink AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml to worktree root. (4) Return worktree path. CleanupAsync: (1) Run git worktree remove .agents/{agentId} --force. (2) Optionally delete the agent branch if no unmerged commits. (3) Log cleanup to AgentEventLog.

BRANCH STRATEGY ENFORCEMENT: Create IAgentBranchStrategy interface with PrepareBranchAsync(workDir, agentId, strategy, ct) -> string (returns branch name) and FinalizeBranchAsync(workDir, agentId, strategy, ct). Implementations: (1) DirectBranchStrategy - no-op, agent commits to current branch. (2) FeatureBranchStrategy - git checkout -b agent/{agentId}/{timestamp} from main/develop, returns branch name. (3) WorktreeBranchStrategy - branch already created by worktree isolation, returns existing branch name. Strategy selected from AgentWorkspaceEntity.BranchStrategyOverride ?? AgentDefinitionEntity.BranchStrategy.

SESSION LOG LINKAGE: (1) Add optional AgentDefinitionId (string, nullable) FK to SessionLogEntity. (2) Add EF migration for the new column. (3) In SessionLogService.SubmitAsync, when SourceType matches a known AgentDefinitionEntity.Id (case-insensitive lookup), populate AgentDefinitionId automatically. (4) Add AgentDefinitionId filter to session log query endpoint. (5) Add navigation property to SessionLogEntity -> AgentDefinitionEntity (optional). This enables queries like: all sessions from agent copilot in workspace X.

AGENT HEALTH MONITOR: Create AgentHealthMonitorService as IHostedService (BackgroundService). On a configurable interval (default 30s), iterate all running agent processes. For each: check Process.HasExited. If exited unexpectedly (non-zero exit code or not user-requested stop): log AgentEventLog with EventType=Exit and exit code, apply restart policy (AgentWorkspaceEntity.RestartPolicy: never/on-failure/always). On restart: re-launch with same config. Cap restarts at configurable max (default 3) with exponential backoff. Log all health check results at Debug level, failures at Warning.

NEW AGENT CONTROLLER ENDPOINTS: Add to AgentController: POST /mcpserver/agents/{agentId}/launch?workspace= (launches agent process), POST /mcpserver/agents/{agentId}/stop?workspace= (stops agent process), GET /mcpserver/agents/{agentId}/process-status?workspace= (gets running process info), GET /mcpserver/agents/running?workspace= (lists all running agents in workspace). All require JWT AgentManager policy. Return AgentProcessInfo DTOs.

NEW AGENT SERVICE METHODS: Add to IAgentService: LaunchAgentAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct), StopAgentAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct), GetAgentProcessStatusAsync(workspacePath, agentId, ct), ListRunningAgentsAsync(workspacePath, ct). These delegate to IAgentProcessManager after resolving config from AgentWorkspaceEntity.

DI REGISTRATION: Register IAgentProcessManager as singleton (manages cross-request process state). Register IAgentIsolationStrategy implementations as named services or strategy factory. Register AgentHealthMonitorService as hosted service. Register IAgentBranchStrategy implementations similarly.

TESTING: (1) AgentProcessManagerTests - mock Process.Start, verify launch/stop/status lifecycle, verify process tracking dictionary. (2) WorktreeIsolationStrategyTests - mock git commands, verify worktree add/remove calls. (3) FeatureBranchStrategyTests - mock git commands, verify branch creation. (4) AgentHealthMonitorTests - mock process status, verify restart logic and backoff. (5) MarkerFileService integration test - verify agentAdditions appear in generated marker. (6) SessionLogService test - verify AgentDefinitionId auto-populated from SourceType. (7) AgentController integration tests - launch/stop/status endpoints.

CONFIGURATION: New appsettings.json sections: Mcp:AgentProcessManager: { AgentsDirectory: ".agents", HealthCheckIntervalSeconds: 30, MaxRestarts: 3, RestartBackoffBaseSeconds: 5 }. Per-workspace agent config already exists in AgentWorkspaceEntity (DB).

description: Implement the runtime behavior layer for per-agent workspace functionality, building on the existing complete data model (AgentDefinitionEntity, AgentWorkspaceEntity, AgentEventLogEntity) and service layer (AgentService, AgentController).
Core capability: Launch, monitor, and stop agent processes per-workspace with workspace-specific configuration overrides (launch command, models, branch strategy, seed prompt, isolation mode).

Agent isolation: Enforce AgentIsolation strategies - worktree mode creates a git worktree per agent, clone mode creates a shallow clone. Agents work in their isolated copy, changes merged back via PR.
Marker file integration: Inject AgentWorkspaceEntity.MarkerAdditions into AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml during marker file generation, allowing per-agent custom instructions.
Session log linkage: Connect SessionLogEntity.SourceType to AgentDefinitionEntity via optional FK, enabling agent-scoped session log queries and audit trails.
Branch management: Enforce BranchStrategy per agent - direct (commit to current branch), feature-branch (create agent-named branch), or worktree (git worktree per agent session).
Health monitoring: Periodic health checks on running agent processes with configurable restart policies (never, on-failure, always).
items.note: Replanned and reopened on 2026-03-10 based on code audit. Existing data model/service CRUD foundations are present (AgentDefinitionEntity, AgentWorkspaceEntity, AgentEventLogEntity, AgentService CRUD, AgentController CRUD/read endpoints, built-in seed defaults), but the runtime per-agent workspace feature set is still missing or incomplete. Missing/partial areas confirmed by audit: (1) agent process lifecycle management (launch/stop/status tracking), (2) enforced isolation strategies (worktree/clone/none), (3) enforced branch strategies, (4) marker file agent additions injection, (5) session-log linkage to agent definition, (6) health monitoring/restart behavior, (7) runtime controller endpoints + tests + docs. This TODO status had drifted and was incorrectly marked done; it is now reopened with a regenerated plan aligned to current code. Retry verification confirmed persisted progress now includes a hand-authored migration file: 20260310213500_AddAgentRuntimeRestartPolicyAndSessionAgentLink.cs.

items.title: [READY] Allow website URL ingestion into GraphRAG without pre-downloading content
technicalDetails: Scope: add first-class website URL ingestion so GraphRAG can index remote pages without pre-staging files in docs/external.
API contract: add a typed request/response for URL ingestion (url, includeSubpages, maxPages, maxDepth, maxBytesPerPage, forceRefresh, triggerGraphRagIndex).
Service design: add a WebsiteIngestor in src\\McpServer.Services\\Ingestion using IHttpClientFactory, with canonical URL normalization and deterministic source keys.
Security: enforce http/https only, block localhost/private/link-local targets, constrain redirects, and cap downloaded bytes/pages to prevent SSRF and resource abuse.
Content extraction: parse HTML to text (strip script/style/nav boilerplate), preserve title + headings, and support non-HTML text payloads via content-type fallback.
Indexing integration: convert fetched pages to ContextDocument/ContextChunk with SourceType=external-web and upsert via IngestionCoordinator using existing embedding/vector flow.
Operational behavior: return per-URL outcome (ingested/skipped/error), total docs/chunks written, and explicit partial-failure diagnostics instead of silent skips.
Transport surface: expose capability in both REST and MCP tools so Director/CLI/agents can ingest website URLs directly.
Client surface: extend McpServer.Client ContextClient + models to call the new endpoint and deserialize ingestion results.
Traceability: add/append FR/TR/TEST mappings for website ingestion and include requirement IDs in new code XML docs and tests.
Docs: update docs/context and user/API docs with request limits, security behavior, and examples for single-page vs bounded crawl ingestion.
Validation: cover unit/integration/client tests and run existing build/tests for Support.Mcp + Client + ingestion-related suites.

items.title: Requirements Management Feature - CRUD + document generation endpoints
technicalDetails: New project component: RequirementsManagementController at src/McpServer.Support.Mcp/Controllers/RequirementsController.cs

IRequirementsRepository - file-backed persistence using SemaphoreSlim for write serialization. Each mutating call updates the in-memory model then atomically writes the affected file via File.WriteAllTextAsync to a temp path followed by File.Replace (atomic swap).

RequirementsDocumentRenderer - RenderFunctional(), RenderTechnical(), RenderTesting(), RenderMapping(), RenderAll(). RenderAll() uses System.IO.Compression.ZipArchive to produce a single in-memory ZIP containing all four files with their canonical filenames.

Sub-resources: POST/GET /mcpserver/requirements/fr, GET/PUT/DELETE /mcpserver/requirements/fr/{id}; same pattern for /tr/{id} and /test/{id}. GET /mcpserver/requirements/mapping for the full table. GET /mcpserver/requirements/generate?doc= for document output.

MCP tools (added to McpServerMcpTools.cs): requirements_generate(doc), requirements_list(type), requirements_create(type, id, title, body), requirements_update(type, id, title?, body?), requirements_delete(type, id).

Document file paths resolved relative to RepoRoot via IOptions<RequirementsOptions>. Default paths: docs/Project/Functional-Requirements.md, docs/Project/Technical-Requirements.md, docs/Project/Testing-Requirements.md, docs/Project/TR-per-FR-Mapping.md. Configurable via Mcp:Requirements:* config section.
All public types require XML doc comments (CS1591 enforced as error in this repo).
ApiKeyAuthFilter is no longer used; all /mcpserver/* routes are protected by WorkspaceAuthMiddleware at the pipeline level. No per-controller auth attributes needed.

Status: APPROVED (operator, 2026-10-10T16:19:44Z: "Plan approved"), after plan-readiness HV round 43 (AGREE, accuracy 99, completeness 98, every claim PASS; receipts committed in 465bf4e2). Before that: NOT APPROVED (operator, 2026-10-09). Execution proceeds step by step from P0 under the gates below. Persisted as MCP TODO `PLAN-SESSIONTURNREVIEW-001` (priority high); handoff `docs/handoffs/sessionturn-review-plan-20261009T022141Z.md`.

Worktree `/home/sharpninja/github/McpServer/.claude/worktrees/session-20261009` (branch `worktree-session-20261009`). Source baseline: `f56dcf70` (== `origin/develop` on 2026-10-09, QBrainAi rename); every source anchor in this plan was verified against it. The branch has since gained only documentation and receipt commits (`git diff --name-only f56dcf70..HEAD` lists only `AGENTS.md`, removed handoff files `CODEX-HANDOFF.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `docs/handoffs/*`, `docs/plans/handoff-*`, `docs/Project/Plugin-Simplification-Handoff.md`, plus `docs/setup/*` and `docs/receipts/*`; no `src/`, `tests/`, `build/`, or `plugins/` change). The approval HEAD is recorded by P0.1 (`git rev-parse HEAD` at approval) and P0.1 re-runs that diff to confirm the baseline still holds. Plugin repo `/home/sharpninja/github/mcpserver-claude-code-plugin` (1.118.0, `d3a07e0`). Plan request turn: `req-20261009T004308Z-prompt-e18e` in session `ClaudeCode-20261009T002615Z-plugin-session`.
## Context
The operator requires an agent self-review and a hostile validation (HV) on every result, plus truthful, per-request audit in the MCP session log. Today:

- Reviews have no structured home. They live in free-text turns, `docs/receipts/hv/*` (integer `accuracy`/`completeness` 0-100), and the unlinked HostileReview subsystem (`double` 0-1). No score in the codebase is a lossless decimal.
- Turn logging is not trustworthy, so anything attached to a turn would attach to the wrong request. Receipts observed in this session (plugin 1.118.0):

- Twin turns per prompt (e.g. `req-20261009T011653Z-prompt-b776` and `-c9a3`): MCP hooks were then registered twice (`~/.claude/settings.json` bridge hooks plus the enabled plugin `mcpserver@mcpserver-local` `hooks/hooks.json`). The bridge hooks were removed later on 2026-10-09 (MEMORY-FACT-003); a read-only check at 2026-10-09T17:54Z found no `hooks` key in `~/.claude/settings.json` or either `settings.local.json`, one plugin install, and one registration per event. The defect that let the duplicate go unreported remains: `validate-claude-mcp-hooks.ps1` wraps the `enabledPlugins` map as one item (line ~72), so it never sees the plugin as enabled and would report `valid` for a duplicate. A2 is therefore a regression fix verified against a fresh live inventory, not a cleanup of a current duplicate. Observed later the same day with hooks active: the prompt hook opens phantom turns for background task notifications, and each such open supersede-cancels the real turn in progress (`req-20261009T175347Z-prompt-dc63`, `req-20261009T175421Z-prompt-79dd`).

## Locked operator decisions (2026-10-09)
Turn logging

- Every user request (including messages queued mid-turn) is exactly one turn; actions and decisions map to the turn of the request that caused them, determined by the write-attribution rule below (D2). Enforcement of turn-logging correctness is Phase A and ships first.
- Plugin turn edits are independent: opening, editing, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn's local or server state; concurrent edits to different turns do not interfere.

- Unsupported-session failsafe (operator, 2026-10-10: "If QBrain is truly not available, use the failsafe already in the plugin." and, choosing between a failsafe capture and a warn-only Stop, "1"): when a host session fails closed under D6 (`unsupportedSince`), the model's session-log writes for a turn that was already open at that moment go to the plugin's existing failsafe instead of being refused (reviews excepted: they keep their no-failsafe rule and are recorded after the drain through the original pair), so the Stop gate's remedy stays accepted; the captured records drain at the next SessionStart through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original pair (C5); every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001).

- Clear-session closing rule (operator, 2026-10-10, choosing option A over leaving blocked and withdrawn turns open: "A"): clear-session completes each turn that meets the completion policy, fails each withdrawn turn (reason "withdrawn before delivery") and each turn the model marks blocked (with its blocker reason; `failed` requires `requestClass` only, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC002), and leaves every other turn in progress, reported by requestId with its exact missing items, never fabricating reviews (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001). Definition (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): "marked blocked" means the turn's `blockers` section (the existing decision-list field, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001) holds at least one nonblank model-authored entry, read by the clear-session coordinator for that turn by its original (`sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, and the first entry is the fail reason; precedence per turn: withdrawn -> `failTurn` ("withdrawn before delivery"); else blocked -> `failTurn` with the blocker reason (blocked takes precedence over a ready completion); else meets the completion policy -> `completeTurn`; else stays in progress, reported with its exact missing items. Close prerequisites (catalog cross-reference, not a change to the decision): before clear-session fails a withdrawn or blocked turn, the model writes by that turn's original pair, within the same clear-session run and before its session-end step, every prerequisite the plugin and the server require for that close, in the Stop gate remedy order (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009): a designDecision when the turn has no model evidence (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002), then a `requestClass` when it is missing or `Unclassified`, judged from the turn's `queryText`; the coordinator then fails the turn with its reason (TR-MCP-CLEARSESSION-001-AC001).

- Request identity (operator D1, 2026-10-09: "have the server issue a request token when a message arrives"): the server mints every turn's `requestId` when a user message arrives (ingress), through the new mint operation `POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint`. The mint call carries an idempotency nonce derived from the host's own identity for that message event (host binding table): a host per-prompt id, or a SHA-256 of host event fields that every delivery of that event carries identically. Every delivery of one event therefore sends the same nonce and receives the same token, including network retries and failsafe replay on every host and, on hosts whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex `turn_id`, grok and grok-bot `promptId`, cline-v2 `runId`, opencode `messageID`) or the bridge's single ordered source (claude-code, claude-cowork), two hook processes started by a doubly registered hook (on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint, and a second new equal-field invocation fails closed); two separate user messages (including two intentionally identical prompts) are two events and receive two tokens. On copilot and classic cline, whose event fields include no per-message id, a message whose session, timestamp, and prompt all equal an already minted one is indistinguishable from a redelivery of it, so the host session fails closed under D6 instead of merging or guessing (host binding table, equal-field rule). The host id is only the idempotency key; the turn identity is the server-issued token. There is no prompt-text dedupe window. Every mint comes from a host arrival mechanism (a prompt hook, the arrival bridge, or a host-native hook adapter); no supported host relies on the model to mint. The stop gate's `duplicate_delivery_suspected` warning is a diagnostic only and is never counted as D1 compliance.

- Queued-message arrival (operator D5, 2026-10-09: "Arrival bridge"): a message the operator sends while a turn is running is minted when it is enqueued, not when the model later processes it. On hosts that record the enqueue in a transcript (Claude Code), a per-host-session arrival bridge started by the SessionStart hook tails the transcript and follows each queued message through the lifecycle the transcript records. Observed in this workspace's Claude Code transcripts on 2026-10-09: 117 `enqueue`, 79 `dequeue`, 35 `remove` (27 with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`), 2 `popAll`; a normal prompt is `enqueue` then `dequeue` within milliseconds, a mid-turn message is `enqueue` then `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn` when it is injected into the running turn (for example the operator's mid-turn message beginning "write a global memory with the" was removed with `absorbed_mid_turn` at 2026-10-09T14:35:47.730Z), and `popAll` pulls queued text back into the input box. The bridge mints at `enqueue` (state `queued`); the request becomes `delivered` at `dequeue` (applied by the bridge from the transcript itself; on hosts with a bridge the prompt hook neither mints nor claims) or at `remove` with `absorbed_mid_turn`; it becomes `withdrawn` at `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason. Task notifications and other system events that the host also enqueues are classified and never minted; on bridge hosts they keep their queue position (`kind: system`), so their `dequeue` never delivers a user request.

- Hosts without an arrival mechanism (operator D6, 2026-10-09: "Adapters or unsupported"): a host is supported for turn logging only through an arrival mechanism this plan specifies (a prompt hook that fires at enqueue, the claude-code/claude-cowork arrival bridge, or the classic-cline native-hook adapter); every other host is unsupported until a separately approved adapter exists, and a queue or enqueue event that P0.2 records on such a host becomes a traced follow-up adapter TODO (filed in P0.8) for operator approval (host binding table). A host with no arrival mechanism is declared unsupported for turn logging until it gains one: its plugin reports `turn_logging_unsupported` on every session-log verb and writes nothing (a host session that becomes unsupported after one of its requests was delivered follows the host binding table unsupported-session rule and the 2026-10-10 failsafe decision), and no first-sight minting is used anywhere.

- Plugin equivalence (operator D7, 2026-10-09, confirmed in chat "1 yes" for the requirement and its qualification posted by Codex in `MEMORY-PROCESS-007` at 17:48:48Z and 17:52:06Z): all QBrain.AI plugins keep equivalent functionality; shared capabilities, contracts, fixes, and behavior changes go to every plugin; host-specific adaptations preserve equivalent supported behavior; equivalence is limited by what each host's plugin infrastructure can support, no extraordinary effort is spent forcing unworkable equivalence, and each such limit is documented as a feature-specific capability limitation instead of being claimed as equivalent. A D6 `turn_logging_unsupported` host is such a documented limitation. The limitations live in `docs/AGENT-PLUGIN-FEATURE-MATRIX.md` (one row per plugin and feature: supported, adapted, or limited, with the reason and the receipt), first written in P0.8 from the P0.2 receipts, updated in A9 and S11, and checked by a docs contract test.

- Write attribution (operator D2, 2026-10-09: tie each write to its request automatically through the agent app's hooks): every verb invocation is bound to one request automatically from host context, without the model naming it: the binding is the write target of the invoking host session at the moment the invocation starts, captured once and stored immutably with that invocation (its persist record and failsafe record), so a later message never retargets an invocation already started. A host session's write target is the request most recently delivered to the model in that host session: a prompt the host hands to the model as a new turn (the prompt hook on hosts without a bridge, or the bridge's `dequeue` delivery), or a queued message absorbed into the running turn (`absorbed_mid_turn`). Minting alone never moves the write target, so work the model is still doing for request R1 after R2 is enqueued stays on R1 until R2 is delivered. Explicit `requestId` remains accepted as an override, for example to continue R1 work after R2 was absorbed, and it is required while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9). Attribution therefore maps each write to the request most recently delivered to the model in its host session when the write started. A write is never attributed by guesswork: when a verb cannot read its host session key from its own invocation context (host binding table), it binds only if exactly one live host session of its agent exists in the workspace (warning `host_session_inferred`); with none it is refused (`host_session_unknown`), and with more than one it is refused (`host_session_ambiguous`), in both cases unless it carries the trusted recovery or review-backfill pair (original MCP `sessionId` and `requestId`, verified against the server for this workspace and agent, C5); an explicit `requestId` alone never lets a verb without a host session key write. No verb ever targets the workspace-level `current-turn.yaml`.

- Ambiguous attribution (operator D9, 2026-10-09: "Refuse when ambiguous"): no host supplies a per-action signal of which request caused a write, so automatic binding applies only while exactly one delivered request is open in the host session. While two or more delivered requests are open (for example R2 absorbed mid-turn while R1 is still open), a write without an explicit `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous`, naming the open requests; the model passes `requestId` until all but one are closed. Writes are never attributed by guesswork.

- Copilot duplicate deliveries (operator D11, 2026-10-09: "Supported only if single hook"): Copilot gives no stable per-prompt id and separately registered hooks may see different `timestamp` values, so Copilot turn logging is supported only while the plugin's duplicate check proves exactly one MCP prompt hook across all Copilot hook sources; otherwise the Copilot prompt hook reports `turn_logging_unsupported` before any mint, and the condition is a D7 documented limitation until fixed. One Copilot prompt therefore never becomes two turns.

Request class

- Turn scalar `requestClass`: `Code` | `Docs` | `Chore` (case-insensitive in, canonical PascalCase out, anything else rejected). Required, enforced at transition to `completed` or `failed`, not at creation (hooks create turns before the agent can classify). Legacy rows backfilled to `Unclassified` (readable; never accepted on new writes from agent surfaces).
Review record (shared by `agentReview` and `hostileReview`)

- Fields: `status` (`Unnecessary` | `Unstarted` | `Running` | `Pass` | `Fail` | `Other`), `otherNotes`, `correctness`, `completeness` (lossless decimal 0..1), `correctnessThreshold`, `completenessThreshold` (server-stamped, read-only), `reasons` (string[]), `reviewer`, `reviewedAt` (UTC), `requestJsonlPath`, `responseJsonlPath`. No `passed` bool.
- One record per kind per turn; latest write wins.

- Server creates both at turn creation as `Unstarted`. `hostileReview` flips to `Unnecessary` when `requestClass` becomes `Chore`, and back to `Unstarted` if the class changes away while still `Unnecessary`. Records past `Unstarted`/`Unnecessary` are never auto-changed. Legacy turns are backfilled `agentReview=Unstarted`, `hostileReview=Unstarted`. (Catalog cross-references, not a change to the decision: the flip and its reverse apply only to in-progress turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-006-AC002 and UC-4; a reset restores the creation default for the turn's current class, FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-001-AC004.)
- `otherNotes` with text is rejected unless `status` is `Other`.

- Strict per-status fields: `Unnecessary`/`Unstarted` carry no scores, reasons, reviewer, timestamps, or paths; `Running` requires `reviewer`, forbids scores; `Pass`/`Fail` require `correctness`, `completeness`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`; `hostileReview` `Pass`/`Fail` also require `requestJsonlPath` and `responseJsonlPath`; `Other` requires non-empty `otherNotes` (the Other reason; operator D4, 2026-10-09: "Other requires Other Reason be populated") and allows optional scores, `reasons`, `reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, and receipt paths. `Unnecessary` is server-managed only.

- Thresholds: `Mcp:SessionLog:ReviewThresholds:{Agent|Hostile}:{Correctness|Completeness}` (decimal 0..1, per instance through `McpInstanceResolver` overrides), default 0.98, inclusive (score >= threshold passes). Pass requires both scores to meet their thresholds. The server derives `Pass`/`Fail`; a supplied `Pass`/`Fail` that contradicts the derivation is rejected (422 `review_status_conflict`); omitting status lets the server derive it. `Other` is never derived. Thresholds in force are stamped on the record.
- Names stay `correctness`/`completeness`. HV tooling maps `accuracy` -> `correctness` and integer percent -> decimal/100.
Completion rules

- `completed` requires `requestClass` plus `agentReview.status` in `Pass`/`Fail`/`Other`; for `Code`/`Docs` also `hostileReview.status` in `Pass`/`Fail`/`Other`; for `Chore` `hostileReview` is not checked (HV not required). `Unstarted`/`Running` block where checked. Pass is not required (Fail/Other complete).
- `failed` requires `requestClass` only. Reviews remain writable on terminal turns.

- Server-internal writers (QuadBrain chat, AuditedAgentCliClient, WorkspacePolicyService, federation replication, transcript/session ingestion) are exempt by code-path origin; they never fabricate reviews.

Host binding table (locks the D1 nonce source, the D5 arrival source, and the D2 host session key per host; every turn token is still minted by the server). Rules common to all hosts:

- Nonce: computed from the event itself, never from the hook process, so every delivery of one event yields the same nonce; a value outside `^[A-Za-z0-9._:-]{1,64}$` is replaced by the 64 lowercase hex characters of its SHA-256. Equal-field rule (copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id): under `turn-open.lock`, a new prompt-hook invocation whose nonce already has a failsafe mint record or a `pending-<nonce>` turn in that host session, or whose mint returns `merged`, cannot be told apart from a separate message with equal session, timestamp, and prompt, so it mints and binds nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 exactly as the bridge does for an unattributable record (`unsupportedSince: { causeNonce, causeOperation: prompt_hook, reason: indistinguishable_arrival }` with the session-level envelope; every session-log verb then reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until the session ends, except that writes for a turn already open at that moment go to the plugin failsafe under the unsupported-session failsafe rule, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001; its open turns are listed at the next SessionStart). A network retry or failsafe replay of a stored mint record is a drain of that record, not a new invocation, and reuses its nonce without failing closed.

- Unsupported-session rule (D6; operator option 1 of 2026-10-10): every check that makes a host session report `turn_logging_unsupported` after one of its requests was delivered records `unsupportedSince` with the session-level envelope in `turn-state.yaml` in the same atomic replace that makes the session unsupported, with `reason` set to that check's code: `queue_removal_ambiguous` (bridge), `indistinguishable_arrival` (equal-field rule), `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` (an unknown queue operation, a record missing a required field, or a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset`), `duplicate_prompt_hook` (the copilot or classic-cline single-registration check starts failing; the first verb or hook in that host session that observes it records it), or, for any other D6 check, its own reason code; plus `causeOffset` or `causeNonce` where the cause has one, else `detectedAtUtc`. Whatever the reason, the unsupported-session failsafe of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 then applies: writes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) are captured, and every mint and every other write is refused. Every user message that reaches a host arrival mechanism (prompt hook, arrival bridge, or host-native hook adapter; D5, D6) maps to exactly one session-log turn whose `requestId` the server mints at ingress (operator D1).

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC001 The plugin opens every turn through the server mint operation (`POST /qbrainai/sessionlog/{agent}/{sessionId}/mint` with an `ingressNonce`, or its client and REPL equivalents, called only by hooks and adapters); the server mints `req-<server UTC yyyyMMddTHHmmssZ>-<8 lowercase hex random>`, opens the turn `in_progress`, and returns the token; the plugin never invents a requestId. A minted requestId is unique within the workspace, enforced by the database for minted turns across all sessions; a violation of that requestId index makes the server generate a new requestId (at most 5 retries after the original attempt, 6 attempts in all, then 500 `mint_collision_exhausted`) and never merges into another turn, while a violation of the nonce index means the same event and returns the existing requestId (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC002) (`MinterCollision_ReturnsDistinctId`, `MintCollision_ConcurrentCrossSession_DistinctIds` on SQLite, PostgreSQL, and SQL Server).  [A1 server, A3 plugin +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC002 Repeating the mint with the same agent, MCP session id, and `ingressNonce` (network retry, two hook processes started for one event, or failsafe replay after an outage) returns the same requestId and opens no second turn (server behavior on every host; on copilot and classic cline the hook applies the equal-field rule to a `merged` result of a new invocation, so it fails the host session closed instead of binding, while a stored mint retry or failsafe drain binds normally). A same-nonce mint for a turn that is already terminal returns `merged` with that `storedStatus`, leaves the status unchanged, and the hook neither makes it the write target nor adds it to the open list or the stop ledger (`Mint_SameNonceTerminalTurn_MergedNotReopened` server side; `PromptHook_SameNonceTerminalTurn_Merged_NotTargetNotOpenNotLedger` plugin side). [A1 server, A3 plugin, A4 plugin write target, open list, and ledger +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC003 Two user messages with identical prompt text (an intentional repeat, at any interval; on copilot and classic cline the equal-field rule governs a repeat that also shares the timestamp) are two events, derive two nonces, and receive two requestIds and two turns; two independent hook processes receiving one event (a doubly registered hook) derive one nonce from the host binding table and receive one requestId on every host whose nonce is a stable per-message id (codex, grok, grok-bot, cline-v2, opencode; on bridge hosts the single bridge per host session mints, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-006); on copilot and classic cline a second registration is refused before any mint (D11 and the classic-cline single-registration check), so the positive two-process case does not apply there. On copilot and classic cline, whose nonce hashes event fields with no per-message id, two messages whose timestamps differ mint two turns, a second new invocation with equal session, timestamp, and prompt cannot be told apart from a separate message, so it mints nothing and the host session fails closed under D6 (`indistinguishable_arrival`) rather than merging or guessing, and a retry or failsafe replay of one stored mint reuses its nonce (`Copilot_SamePromptDifferentTimestamp_TwoMints`, `Copilot_EqualFieldsSecondInvocation_FailsClosed_NoSecondMint`, `Copilot_MintRetryAndFailsafeReplay_ReuseNonce_NoFailClose`, `Cline_SamePromptDifferentTimestamp_TwoMints`, `Cline_EqualFieldsSecondInvocation_FailsClosed_NoSecondMint`, `Cline_MintRetryAndFailsafeReplay_ReuseNonce_NoFailClose`). [A1 server, A3 plugin, A8 Node hosts +A4 +A9]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC004 Distinct prompts open distinct turns. [A3 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC005 A message delivered while another turn is in progress (queued or mid-turn) gets its own turn, minted by the host's arrival mechanism (arrival bridge, prompt hook, or host-native hook adapter); the running turn is not changed. [A4]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC006 The Claude hook validator reports `duplicate` when an MCP hook script is registered by both `~/.claude/settings.json` and the enabled plugin, repairs it with a backup, and `-CheckOnly` never mutates settings. [A2]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC007 The hook installer adds no bridge hook for an event the enabled plugin already covers. [A2]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC008 When the server is unreachable at ingress, the hook persists a failsafe mint record carrying its nonce and opens a provisional local turn `pending-<nonce>`; on failsafe drain the server mints idempotently from the nonce and the plugin rebinds the provisional turn and every write bound to it to the minted requestId, in original order. Either id resolves to the same turn; a crash at any point during the rebind loses no write and creates no second turn; a committed pending-to-minted alias stays discoverable and is reapplied until every consumer of it (including an audit outbox) durably acknowledges it, and duplicate delivery or application is harmless (C2). With two or more consumers, an alias acknowledged by one stays discoverable to the others; replay to a consumer stops only after that consumer durably acknowledges, and stops entirely once all have. No server turn ever has a `pending-` requestId: a write captured under a pending id and sent after the alias is sent under the minted id, and the writes of one turn reach the server in their original order even when a close of that turn was made while earlier writes waited in the failsafe. A mint that the server or REPL does not support is recognized only by the trusted mint adapter (PowerShell A3, Node A8) for the exact mint operation, from either an authenticated, bound mint-endpoint response with HTTP 404 and no detail code, or the structured `unknown_method` (GenericClientPassthrough) or `method_not_found` (ReplCommandDispatcher) result for the expected mint verb, as on a server older than A1; it is never inferred from prose, malformed detail metadata, arbitrary 404s, or unrelated operations, keeps the original structured cause, and is classified as a transport outage by that adapter only (never by the generic C9 classifier or the audit outbox in-call retry loop) and handled like one (failsafe retained, turn stays `pending-<nonce>`, retried at a later drain); a mint refused for a final reason (404 with detail code `session_not_open`, 400 validation) reports `turn-open-failed` with the server code, keeps its failsafe record marked final and not retried, invents no requestId, and the stop gate warns naming the prompt. On drain the plugin first replays an idempotent session open for the record's envelope `mcpSessionId` (an outage that spanned SessionStart left that session unopened on the server), then the mint; a `session_not_open` refusal is final only after that session open is confirmed (`OutageSpanningSessionStart_DrainOpensSessionThenMints_NotFinal`). The pending-to-minted lookup entry is permanent for the life of the plugin cache: retiring an alias's consumer-delivery obligation after the last required acknowledgement never removes it, so a reader holding the pending id resolves the minted turn after every acknowledgement and after a restart. After the delivery obligation is retired, `getAlias` still returns the full agreed record with the exact final acknowledgement set, and a repeated acknowledgement is an idempotent no-op. [A3 +A5 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009 Arrival bridge (D5): on claude-code, and on claude-cowork when P0.2 shows Cowork runs plugin hooks and passes the same bridge probes as claude-code (otherwise FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008-AC004 applies: Cowork reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and the feature matrix records the limitation), the arrival bridge is the only minter: every user message is minted from its transcript `enqueue` record (nonce `q-` from that record) before the model processes it, in state `queued`, and the prompt hook neither mints nor claims, so no hook-to-bridge correlation exists to fail (Claude Code's `queue-operation` records carry no parent `promptId`; the plan never correlates across record kinds without a shared key). One message yields exactly one mint for every prompt form P0.2 captures (plain, slash command, attachment or image, image-only, multi-line CRLF, non-ASCII, at least 1 MiB), and two messages with equal text yield two mints. A pid file naming a dead or foreign process does not prevent a bridge start; a host session ended by the idle rule (`ended.yaml` with `reason: idle`) is live again at its next mint or keyed verb from that host session key, which removes the marker in the same atomic replace under `turn-open.lock` before acting; a keyed verb that revives a session with no delivered request is then refused with `request_unknown` (no write target); a `reason: session_end` marker never revives (`IdleEnded_KeyedVerb_RevivesAtomically_NoTargetRequestUnknown`, `IdleEnded_Revival_CrashRestart_Consistent`, `SessionEndMarker_NeverRevives`); a resumed or forked transcript mints nothing for queue records written before that host session's SessionStart; a transcript shorter than `appliedThroughOffset` is reported with `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, changes no queue entry, records `unsupportedSince` with that reason after a delivered request (unsupported-session rule), and the host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported`, with writes for its already open turns going to the plugin failsafe, until the bridge restarts on a valid transcript (fail closed, like an unknown record shape); the bridge restarts from SessionStart after `/clear` and resume and stops at SessionEnd. If P0.2 shows a user prompt that produces no `enqueue` record, or a `dequeue` that does not take the head, the host is `turn_logging_unsupported` (D6) (`ClaudeCode_P0_2NotPassed_TurnLoggingUnsupported_ZeroMintsZeroWrites`; the real prompt-form fixture case runs only when those probes pass). [A3 +A4]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC010 Queue lifecycle: a `queued` request becomes `delivered` (and the host session's write target) at `dequeue` (the head of the queue) or at `remove` with reason `absorbed_mid_turn`, and becomes `withdrawn` at a `popAll` or a `remove` with any other or no reason; minting never moves the write target; a withdrawn request stays `in_progress` on the server until the model closes it (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009). A record that cannot be attributed to exactly one queued entry (equal content with no shared key: a `remove` matching two or more entries, or a `popAll` carrying fewer lines of a content than there are matching entries) is never guessed: the host session fails closed under D6 (the bridge stops before the record, `unsupportedSince` is recorded, every session-log verb in that host session reports `turn_logging_unsupported` and writes nothing to the server until it ends, writes for its already open turns go to the plugin failsafe and drain at the next SessionStart (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001), and its open turns are listed with their pairs at the next SessionStart); a `popAll` whose line count equals the matching entry count withdraws them all. Every `enqueue` takes a queue position: system events as unminted `kind: system` entries, so a `dequeue` whose head is a system entry delivers nothing and the user request behind it stays `queued` until its own delivery (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001). [A3 +A4]
FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002 Background and system events never open turns.

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC001 Prompts that are `<task-notification>`, `<local-command-*>`, `<agent-message ...>` subagent hand-backs, or only system-reminder blocks, payloads marking a subagent (Claude Code `agent_id`, Grok `subagentType`), and deliveries with `MCP_SUBAGENT_ID`/`GROK_SUBAGENT_ID` set open no turn, call no mint, leave turn state unchanged, and report `system-event-skipped`; classification uses these structural markers only, never the topic or wording of the prompt. On every supported host a prompt event produced by a subagent or a child session (for example an opencode `task` child session's `chat.message`) opens no turn; P0.2 records each host's subagent marker, and a host without one records the limitation in the feature matrix. On bridge hosts a system-event `enqueue` still occupies a queue position (`kind: system`), so its later `dequeue` or removal never delivers or withdraws a user request (`Bridge_SystemEnqueueAheadOfUser_SystemDequeue_UserStaysQueued`, `Bridge_SystemEnqueue_Removed_NoTurn`, `Bridge_SystemAndUserInterleaved_CrashReplay_ZeroWrongTurnWrites`; the `MCP_SUBAGENT_ID`/`GROK_SUBAGENT_ID` deliveries `SystemEvents_SubagentEnvMarkers_NoMint`; the opencode child session `opencodeChildSession_chatMessage_noTurn`). [A3 +A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC002 Slash-command (`<command-name>`) and `<user_query>` prompts open turns, and so does any user prompt that happens to contain a hostile-review or delegation brief (for example the brief that launches a Codex hostile reviewer, which needs its own reviewer turn). [A3 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-002-AC003 Hooks of subagents or parallel sessions sharing the workspace cache never change this session's turn state. [A4 +A8]
FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 A new prompt never cancels an in-progress turn.
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC001 Opening a turn never persists `canceled` for any other turn. [A4 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC002 The prior in-progress turn stays `in_progress` locally and on the server and remains addressable by requestId. [A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004 The stop ledger lists every request delivered since the last passing Stop, plus every earlier entry whose close the server has not confirmed; a request that is minted but still `queued` is not in it until it is delivered (the single enrollment rule of FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001). Only a server-confirmed close leaves the ledger (A5 outcome mapping, `CloseVerb_OnlyServerConfirmedClose_LeavesOpenListAndLedger`), and the Stop gate evaluates that ledger plus one separate scan of `withdrawn` queue entries still `in_progress` (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006 AC-005), so a request withdrawn before delivery is blocked as `turn_withdrawn_unclosed` without ever entering the ledger (A7, `StopGate_LedgerListsDeliveredSinceLastPass_PlusUnconfirmedCloses`, `StopGate_WithdrawnBeforeDelivery_EmptyLedger_BlocksWithdrawnUnclosed_FailByPair_NextStopPasses`). [A4 +A5 +A7]
FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004 Truthful persist outcomes.

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC001 Session submit returns a per-turn outcome, exactly one of `created`, `merged`, or `skipped_terminal`, with `storedStatus` and `reason` on REST, MCP `sessionlog_submit`, and the typed client; there is no `skipped_duplicate` outcome on any surface (operator, 2026-10-09: "Remove"); a resubmit identical to the stored turn reports `merged` with reason `no_change`; duplicate entries for one requestId in one submission are applied last-wins (today's behavior) and report one outcome for that requestId. [A1]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC002 The plugin maps `skipped_terminal` to `persisted:false`, code `skipped_terminal`, non-zero exit, and a cleared failsafe record. [A5 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC003 Omitted-status enrichment and review-section writes on terminal turns report `merged` or success (review-section writes from S4, `SessionLogTurnReviewSectionTests.SectionPut_TerminalTurn_ReportsSuccess`). [A1 +S4]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC004 A plugin verb targeting a locally terminal turn is refused with `turn_immutable` without a server call, except `recordReview` and requestClass-only updates (the exception from S8 and S9, when those verbs ship: `TerminalTurn_RecordReviewAndClassOnly_Accepted_OtherVerbsTurnImmutable`, `terminalTurn_recordReviewAndClassOnly_accepted_otherVerbsTurnImmutable`). [A5 +A8 +S8 +S9]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC005 A result from a server without per-turn outcomes is reported `outcomeVerified:false`. [A5 +A8]
FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005 The stop gate enforces and never closes turns.

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 Blocks with `turn_in_progress` when a delivered request in the stop ledger (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003-AC004) is still in progress; a withdrawn request still in progress blocks under AC009, and a minted request still `queued` only warns. A request in state `queued` (minted, not yet delivered) never produces `turn_in_progress`; the gate warns, naming its requestId and enqueue time. A Stop in one host session never blocks or warns on another host session's turns (`StopGate_OtherHostSession_NeverBlocksOrWarns`). A request enters the stop ledger when it is delivered, so a request minted before a passing Stop and delivered after it is evaluated at the next Stop (`StopGate_EnqueueR2_PassForR1_DequeueR2_NextStopBlocksUntilClosed`, including a restart between the two Stops). Unsupported-session failsafe: in a host session with `unsupportedSince` (whatever its reason, host binding table unsupported-session rule), every session-log write the model makes for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning) (evidence actions, design decisions, `requestClass`, and the close call; a review is never captured, keeping the no-failsafe rule of TR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-005 AC-002 and S9, and is refused with `turn_logging_unsupported`) is captured as a plugin failsafe record that carries the turn's C4 binding and root-id envelope, is marked `unsupported_session`, and is never sent to the server during that host session; every mint and every write for any other turn stays refused with `turn_logging_unsupported` and captures nothing (`UnsupportedSession_MintOrWriteForOtherTurn_Refused_NothingCaptured`). The Stop gate evaluates such a turn with its captured records counted: it blocks until the model's close is captured, with a remedy that names only the missing model evidence, the missing `requestClass` (from S8/S9, when the plugin's requestClass verb ships; a class write is captured like any other write), and the close call (all accepted, AC002; the plugin pre-check lets that close through, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC002), because only the completion gate's terminal reviews cannot be written in that session; it then only warns with the cause and the retained failsafe records. The completion gate is judged at the drain: the server's gate judges the drained close, and a gate rejection keeps the turn in progress and listed with its original pair at that SessionStart, where its reviews are recorded through the C5 pair (FR-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-002-AC002) before it is closed (`UnsupportedSession_ReviewRefused_NotCaptured`, `UnsupportedSession_CodeTurn_DrainedCloseRejectedByGate_StaysListed_ReviewViaPair_ThenCloses`). The next SessionStart for the agent drains the captured records in original order through the trusted recovery flow with the turn's original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair (C5); a record whose turn is no longer in progress on the server is retained and warned, never forced. Each reason is covered from an earlier open turn (`StopGate_UnknownBridgeRecord_EarlierOpenTurn_CloseCaptured_ThenWarnsOnly`, `StopGate_TruncatedTranscript_EarlierOpenTurn_CloseCaptured_ThenWarnsOnly`, `StopGate_SyntheticUnsupportedSince_AnyReason_EarlierOpenTurn_CloseCaptured_ThenWarnsOnly` in A7; the real duplicate-hook transition `DuplicateHookAfterDelivery_UnsupportedSince_OpenTurnCloseCaptured` for copilot in A9 and `nodeDuplicateHookAfterDelivery_unsupportedSince_openTurnCloseCaptured` for classic cline in A8). A withdrawn-before-delivery turn is covered too: its decision, its `requestClass` (from S8/S9), and `failTurn` by original pair are captured, the next Stop warns instead of blocking, and the drain closes it (after S10 the server gate accepts that fail, which needs only the class) (`StopGate_WithdrawnBeforeDelivery_ThenUnsupported_CloseCapturedByPair_NextStopWarns_DrainCloses`). A Stop in another live host session still blocks on that session's own turns (`StopGate_EqualFieldFailClosed_EarlierOpenTurn_CloseCapturedToFailsafe_ThenWarnsOnly_DrainsWithOriginalPair`, `StopGate_BridgeAmbiguity_EarlierOpenTurn_CloseCapturedToFailsafe_ThenWarnsOnly_DrainsWithOriginalPair`). Outage close: a model close held in the ordinary plugin failsafe because of a transport outage turns that turn's block into the existing degraded persistence warning (AC005); its ledger entry stays until the server confirms the close (`StopGate_OutageCloseQueued_WarnsDegraded_LedgerKeptUntilConfirmed`). [A7 +A8 +A9 +S8 +S9 +S10]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002 The plugin close verbs refuse to close a turn that has no model-authored action, design decision, or commit (the evidence predicate TR-MCP-PLUGIN-011-AC003 keeps), with code `turn_missing_model_evidence`; the turn stays in progress, so the stop gate blocks it as `turn_in_progress` with the accumulated remedy of the wire contract (every unmet prerequisite, then the valid close call). A turn closed without model evidence by another surface accepts no plugin edit, so the gate reports it as a warning naming it and never blocks on it. Every stop-gate block names a remedy the plugin accepts on the blocked turn's current status (`StopGate_EveryBlockRemedy_AcceptedOnBlockedTurnStatus`, `CloseVerb_NoEvidence_Refused_TurnStaysInProgress`, `StopGate_ClosedWithoutEvidenceElsewhere_WarnsOnly`, `CloseVerb_CommitOnlyEvidence_Accepted`). [A7 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC003 Blocks with `session_turn_completion_gate` a turn whose most recent close the server refused with that code (recorded locally from the server response; such a turn is still in progress), naming the server's missing items first in its remedy (`StopGate_ServerGateRefusal_BlocksWithServerMissingItems`), except for an already open turn of a host session with `unsupportedSince`, whose completion gate is judged at the drain (AC001). There is no marker condition: the server gate (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002) is the only completion authority. Its remedy is the accumulated per-turn remedy of the wire contract, so it also names any missing model evidence. [S8 +S9 +S10]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC004 Never calls `completeTurn` or `failTurn`. [A7 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC005 Warns without blocking for model-canceled turns, retained failsafe records, and degraded persistence. The warning list is exactly: model-canceled turns, `queue_removal_ambiguous`, `indistinguishable_arrival`, and `duplicate_prompt_hook` (each, and `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized` when it set `unsupportedSince`, or any other `unsupportedSince` reason, naming the open turns of its fail-closed host session and their captured `unsupported_session` failsafe records), queued undelivered requests, retained failsafe records (including final mint refusals and unbound legacy records), degraded persistence, `duplicate_delivery_suspected`, `nonce_source_missing`, `arrival_bridge_format_unrecognized`, `stop_gate_overridden_by_host`, open turns of ended host sessions, a turn closed without model evidence by another surface, a live host session whose arrival bridge is not running, and a turn in progress in the legacy `current-turn.yaml` at upgrade (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC004, `StopGate_LegacyCurrentTurnInProgress_Warned`). [A7]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC006 Passes and clears the ledger only when every check passes. Every Stop invocation re-evaluates the ledger, including when the host reports that an earlier Stop already blocked (Claude Code `stop_hook_active`, Grok `stopHookActive`): while any turn remains open it blocks again with the same findings. If the host ends the session anyway (its own continuation limit), the gate records `stop_gate_overridden_by_host` with the open turn ids in the ledger, and the next SessionStart or prompt hook shows it as a warning until the model closes those turns. A ledger entry whose closing write the server has not confirmed terminal stays in the ledger across passing Stops until the server reports it terminal. Turns still in progress when their host session ends (any reason, including `/clear` and a host override) stay in progress and are listed at the next SessionStart for that agent in the workspace with their original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pairs; closing one through the trusted recovery flow with that pair succeeds, and a `requestId` alone is refused (C5). [A7 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC007 The existing failed-build block is retained. [A7]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC008 Warns (never merges, never blocks) with `duplicate_delivery_suspected` when one host session minted two requestIds within 2 seconds for prompts whose SHA-256 of the normalized text is equal, naming both requestIds so the operator can check hook registration; the warning is diagnostic only (it can fire only where a host's event identity is weaker than expected) and is not evidence of D1 compliance. [A7]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC009 Blocks with `turn_withdrawn_unclosed` while a `withdrawn` request is still `in_progress`, naming it, its withdrawal record (`popAll` or `remove` reason), and the action: close it with `workflow.sessionlog.failTurn` (`requestId` override, reason "withdrawn before delivery"); hooks still never close it. The instruction text includes a designDecision and, from S8/S9 (when the plugin's requestClass and recordReview verbs ship), the `requestClass` the close needs, so following it exactly makes the next Stop pass (`StopGate_WithdrawnFailedPerInstruction_NextStopPasses`). [A7]
FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006 Decision lists through workflow verbs.
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC001 `updateTurn`, `appendActions`, `completeTurn`, `failTurn` accept `designDecisions`, `requirementsDiscovered`, `blockers` and persist them. [A6 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC002 Those lists are part of the dedupe fingerprint, so a change to only them is persisted. [A6]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC003 Model-evidence counters count only model-invoked verbs, never hook-invoked ones (Node core: `nodeHookAuthoredWrites_notEvidence`). [A6 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-006-AC004 One decision call (`appendDecisions`, or a decision passed to `updateTurn`/`completeTurn`/`failTurn`) writes the workspace triple (C7): a `designDecisions` entry, a dialog item with category `decision`, and a `design_decision` action; replaying the same call adds nothing. FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007 Independent turn edits.

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC001 Each turn has its own state file and lock; each host session has one state file `sessions/<hostSessionKey>/turn-state.yaml` holding its write target (the request most recently delivered to the model; D9 refuses unqualified writes while several delivered requests are open), its open delivered requests, its queue (minted requests with `queued`/`delivered`/`withdrawn` state), `appliedThroughOffset`, and the host session's own `mcpSessionId` that its SessionStart records (Node: `turn-state.json`, recorded by the first ingress event for that host session key, because the Node hosts have no SessionStart event), always replaced atomically (temp file, flush, rename) under `turn-open.lock`; `current-turn.yaml` remains only as a read-only legacy status file that no verb uses for targeting. The arrival bridge, the mint, and every verb read the MCP session id only from their own host session's turn-state; the workspace-level `session-state.yaml` is a legacy file never used for targeting, and the rotated-sessionId rebind (`repl-invoke.ps1:1954-1965`, TR-MCP-PLUGIN-012) is never applied to per-turn files, so a second host session's SessionStart never retargets the first (`TwoHostSessions_OwnMcpSessionIds_SecondSessionStartNeverRetargetsFirst`, Node `twoHostSessions_ownMcpSessionIds_secondSessionStartNeverRetargetsFirst`). [A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC002 Every verb resolves exactly one target turn, in this precedence: explicit `requestId` override, else the invocation's bound request, which is refused with `request_ambiguous` while two or more delivered requests are open in the host session (D9); it mutates only that turn; an explicit requestId resolves to exactly one immutable owning MCP session within the validated workspace and agent, and naming a turn of an earlier host session requires its original (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair, used only by recovery and review backfill (C5); an unknown explicit requestId is refused with `request_unknown`, and a terminal one with `turn_immutable` (except the review and class writes allowed on terminal turns, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-004-AC004). A verb whose host session has no delivered request (no write target) is refused with `request_unknown` naming the host session key and writes nothing (`Binding_NoWriteTarget_RequestUnknown_NamesHostSessionKey`). A `request_ambiguous` refusal lists each open delivered request's requestId, delivery time, source, and title. [A4 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC003 Concurrent edits to two turns from separate processes lose nothing and cross-contaminate nothing. [A4 +A8]

A failsafe record without a captured binding (written before the upgrade) is never replayed automatically: it is retained and listed with its path by the stop gate's retained-failsafe warning; a turn in progress in the legacy `current-turn.yaml` at upgrade is listed as a warning by the first SessionStart or Stop and stays addressable by explicit requestId (`Failsafe_LegacyUnbound_NeverAutoReplayed_Retained`, `LegacyCurrentTurnInProgress_ListedAtFirstSessionStart_AddressableByRequestId` in A4; the Stop warnings `StopGate_UnboundLegacyFailsafe_WarnedWithPath`, `StopGate_LegacyCurrentTurnInProgress_Warned` in A7). [A4 +A7 +A8]
- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC005 Opening, closing, or canceling one turn never changes another turn locally or on the server. [A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC006 Host-context binding (operator D2): at the start of each verb invocation the plugin resolves the invoking host session's key by the host's locked method (see the host binding table) and binds the invocation to that host session's write target; the binding is written into the invocation's persist and failsafe records and never re-resolved, so a prompt minted after the invocation started never retargets it. On hosts with an arrival bridge, the invocation records the transcript length when it starts and then applies, under `turn-open.lock`, exactly the transcript records that end at or before that length (records appended after it started are left for later invocations), so the binding is the invocation-start snapshot D2 requires, so its binding reflects every delivery recorded before it began. [A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC007 Interleaving: with R1 delivered and R2 enqueued mid-turn in the same host session, a verb started after R2's mint but before R2's delivery (`absorbed_mid_turn` or `dequeue`) writes to R1; a verb started after R2's delivery without `requestId` is refused with `request_ambiguous` while R1 and R2 are both open (D9); with explicit ids an R1, R2, R1 sequence of writes lands on R1, R2, R1 respectively; once R1 is closed an unqualified verb writes to R2; a withdrawn R2 never becomes a write target; R1 stays in progress throughout. When the verb cannot read its host session key, the live-session rule applies: with exactly one live host session of its agent it binds there with warning `host_session_inferred`; with none or several it is refused (`host_session_unknown`, `host_session_ambiguous`) unless it carries the trusted (MCP `sessionId`, `requestId`) pair of C5 that the server verifies for this workspace and agent; a `requestId` alone is refused the same way; with two concurrent host sessions in one workspace and no keys, zero writes land on the wrong turn. After a prompt's open fails (`turn-open-contended`, `turn-open-failed`, `nonce_source_missing`), unqualified verbs in that host session are refused with `request_unknown` until a later delivery succeeds, so that prompt's work never lands on the earlier turn (`Binding_AfterFailedOpen_UnqualifiedVerb_RequestUnknown`). A turn the server reports terminal, whichever surface closed it, stops counting as an open delivered request at the next verb or Stop, and a request leaves the open list only when the server confirms its close (a queued, refused, or failed close leaves it open; A5 outcome mapping `CloseVerb_OnlyServerConfirmedClose_LeavesOpenListAndLedger`, A7 Stop `StopGate_TurnClosedElsewhere_DroppedFromOpenList`). When the write target is closed while an earlier delivered request is still open, an unqualified verb is refused with `turn_immutable` naming the open request (`Binding_WriteTargetClosed_EarlierStillOpen_TurnImmutable`). [A4 +A5 +A7 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC008 Session changes in place never misattribute: after Claude Code `/clear`, a shell verb binds to the new session's write target (its `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is updated), a long-lived process resolves per call by the live-session rule (the cleared session is ended by SessionEnd reason `clear`), and after resume the resumed session's key is used. [A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC009 Every record family the plugins write for a turn (queue entry, alias, failsafe record, stop-ledger entry inside `turn-state.yaml`, persisted or queued event) carries the root-id envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey, ingressNonce, requestId }` (`requestId` may be the pending alias until rebind), while a session-scoped record that belongs to no turn (a `kind: system` queue entry, `unsupportedSince`) carries the session-level envelope `{ workspacePath, agent, mcpSessionId, hostSessionKey }` plus its own key (`enqueueOffset`, `causeOffset`, on a prompt-hook host `causeNonce`, or, for a cause with neither, its `reason` and `detectedAtUtc`), never an invented nonce or requestId, so each record is attributable on its own without consulting another record (operator, 2026-10-09: "The root id of whatever something is a child of or depends on, should always be carried."; design principle: "Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities."); each family is read back after write and after replay with the envelope intact (`RootIds_EveryRecordFamily_PresentAfterWriteAndReplay`, Node `rootIds every record family present after write and replay`, including the alias and an outbox event). [A3 +A4 +A8]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC002 The local pre-check is advisory: before the close is sent it computes the missing completion items with the exact gate message (the golden-contract rules) and reports them as a warning; it never refuses a close. A class or review recorded by another process, host session, or surface before the completion is honored and is not reported missing. The server gate (FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002, S10) is the only completion authority, so nothing refuses a close that a pre-S10 or rolled-back server would accept, and no activation signal is needed: this plan adds no marker field, and the marker and its signature stay exactly as they are (FR-MCP-140, TR-MCP-SEC-005, TEST-MCP-189 unaffected). When the server refuses a close with 400 `session_turn_completion_gate`, the surface reports the server's message and missing items, the turn stays in progress, and AC003 applies (`Precheck_Advisory_WarnsMissingItems_NeverRefuses`, `nodePrecheck_advisory_warnsMissingItems_neverRefuses`). Unsupported session (operator option 1, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001): for a turn of that host session still in progress when `unsupportedSince` was recorded (a delivered open request, or a `withdrawn` queue entry still `in_progress`, addressed by its original pair; a minted request still `queued` is not covered and stays a warning), the close goes to the `unsupported_session` failsafe with no server write per FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC001 (the advisory warning still prints), and the server gate judges it at the drain; the model-evidence check (FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-005-AC002) still applies. This is plugin-core state only; the McpAgent pre-check of TR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004 has no host session (`Precheck_UnsupportedSession_CodeTurnMissingReviews_CloseCaptured_NoServerWrite`, `nodePrecheck_unsupportedSession_codeTurnMissingReviews_closeCaptured`). [S8 +S9 +S10]

- FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004-AC003 A close that carries actions, decisions, requirements, or blockers is sent as two writes: the carried evidence first, as an additive write that changes no status (so the completion gate never applies to it, FR-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-002-AC004) and is verified by readback, then the status transition. The failsafe keeps each part until that part is verified on the server, so a crash between them replays only what is missing and replay is idempotent. A server gate rejection of the transition therefore loses no evidence: it clears only the transition part, leaves the turn in progress, and reports the refusal with the server's missing items (`CloseWithEvidence_EvidenceWriteVerifiedBeforeTransition_GateRefusalLosesNothing`, `closeWithEvidence_evidenceWriteVerifiedBeforeTransition_gateRefusalLosesNothing` against a server double in S8/S9; `RealGate_RejectedCloseEvidence_SurvivesRestart_ReadBackEveryField`, `realGate_rejectedCloseEvidence_survivesRestart_readBackEveryField` against the real gate in S10). This includes a drained `unsupported_session` close: its `session_turn_completion_gate` rejection clears that failsafe record and keeps the turn in progress and listed with its original pair. The close's carried writes follow this rule until its reviews are recorded through the C5 pair and a later close is accepted (`UnsupportedSession_CodeTurn_DrainedCloseRejectedByGate_StaysListed_ReviewViaPair_ThenCloses`, `nodeUnsupportedSession_codeTurn_drainRejected_reviewViaPair_thenCloses`, run against the real gate in S10). Each TEST id mirrors its TR. P0 creates each record with the title and statement below (exactly: the title is the row text after its id up to ` Tests:`, without its final period; in the statement, <AC list> is the row's Validates and Also validates lists with ranges such as AC001..AC004 expanded, and <test classes> is its Tests: list); the statement is "Validates <AC list> with <test classes>; every listed new or changed AC has a RED receipt before implementation and a green receipt at the slice gate, and every listed baseline-green AC has a green receipt." Every record carries the same three ACs, with its own id prefix: `<TESTID>-AC001` every listed new or changed FR and TR AC has at least one named test that failed (RED) before implementation and passes after, and every listed baseline-green AC has a named test that passes; `<TESTID>-AC002` the mocks-green run and its negative check are recorded on the slice TODO; `<TESTID>-AC003` the listed suites run with zero failures and zero skips in the slice gate. (TEST-SUPPORT-024 uses `ac-1`..`ac-3` with the same texts, matching its family.) Span and satisfaction: a TEST record belongs to the slices in its TR's bracket, every slice labelled in parentheses in its row (for example `(S5)`), and every slice, earlier or later, whose task line names one of its cases or test suites. So TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-008 spans S1, S5, S6, S8, S9, and S10 (S5 and S6 name its golden-map case, S10 its real-gate cases), TEST-MCP-SESSIONREVIEW-009 spans S8, S9, and S11 (whose task names `SessionLogReviewDocsContractTests`), and TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-001 spans S1, S3, S4, S5, and S6. Each slice's gate runs the cases that slice owns plus those of every earlier slice in the span, and the record's three ACs are set satisfied only when the last slice of its span completes. Every case a row names is owned by a slice of that span. Where an AC's bracket names several surfaces, each TEST covers the surfaces its own span implements, and the other surfaces are covered by the TESTs of the slices that implement them (a row says so explicitly where it hands one off, as in "via TEST-MCP-SESSIONCLASS-004").
